months.intro: ICSE 2027 decisions: bound propagation for neural networks, with local nonlinear substitution used to bound activation functions.

papers.title: Local Nonlinear Substitution for Bounding Activation Functions

months.label: September 2026
months.intro: NeurIPS 2026 decisions: randomized smoothing and probabilistic certificates lead, from clustered smoothing for stochastic predictors to early stopping and cheap proxy certificates. Branch-and-bound verification gains combinatorial ℓ0 search in FocusBranch and reinforcement-learned branching, while neural control work certifies observers, safe RL and monotone systems; PANDA brings zero-knowledge proofs to robustness and fairness guarantees, alongside complexity results for narrow networks and Transformers.

papers.title: Affine-Image Propagation for Tight and Scalable Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Tightens ℓ2 robustness verification of networks without Lipschitz regularization via affine-image SDP-CROWN, which bounds preactivations with affine-image constraints relaxed to scaled diagonal-dominance conditions for GPU use; verified accuracy rises 17–57.5% on five MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks, 27–63.5% with branch-and-bound.

papers.title: CAST: Certifiable Aggregation of Smoothed Teachers for Robust Policy Adaptation
Certification from Examples is Hard for Circuits and Transformers under Minimal Overparametrization
papers.summary: Proves that certifying a learned model equals its target from labeled examples can require exponentially many examples: one extra gate in threshold circuits of depth 2 or more, or constant overhead in log-precision Transformers, suffices; on binary addition, wrong models survive extensive checks.

papers.title: Certified Robust Interpretability via Concept-Space Stability under Interventional Proxies
Certified but Private: Scalable Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Neural Network Guarantees
papers.summary: PANDA proves robustness and fairness of a neural network with zero-knowledge proofs while keeping its weights private, by proving CROWN's linear relaxation bounds for activations; it proves local robustness of networks above 2.9M parameters in 5 minutes, about 4 orders of magnitude beyond earlier ZKP systems.

papers.title: Clustered Randomized Smoothing for Stochastic Prediction Functions
papers.summary: Clustered α-smoothing certifies stochastic multi-modal regressors by clustering noisy samples, smoothing within each cluster and mixing the results, bounding the probability that predictions land in mode regions; it lowers Wasserstein distance 27% in trajectory prediction and collision rate 90% in quadrotor control.

papers.title: Do Feature Interactions Break Explainability? Provable Explanations for Any-Order Neural Additive Models
papers.summary: Studies provably minimal sufficient explanations for neural additive models with feature interactions: the problem is Σ2P-hard even at constant order, but sparse interactions or an interaction-aware sufficiency notion make it tractable, yielding smaller, faster explanations from more accurate models than standard NAMs.

papers.title: End-to-End Verification of Neuro-symbolic Automata via Contrastive Logit-Gaps
Ensuring Deployment-Time Safety of Neural Network Controlled Systems via Localized Certificate Repair
FLIP: Fast and Accurate Global Lipschitz Estimation for Large Feedforward Networks
FocusBranch: Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound for $\ell_0$ Neural Network Robustness Verification
papers.summary: FocusBranch verifies ℓ0 local robustness by combinatorial branch-and-bound over nodes defined by a focus pixel set and a level, branching through upper shadows or covering designs and picking a strategy by sampling; it outperforms existing verifiers on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 classifiers.

papers.title: Halt Fast! Early Stopping for Certified Robustness
papers.summary: Speeds up randomized smoothing certification with anytime-valid sequential testing: a lightweight meta-learner predicts image-specific priors for an E-process, cutting sample complexity 20-fold while keeping statistical guarantees and allowing compute to be allocated by application risk thresholds.

papers.title: Iterated Narrow Networks: Turing Completeness at Width 4 on Convex Input Spaces and the Complexity of Verification
papers.summary: Shows that iterating a fixed width-4 ReLU network can simulate any Turing machine on the convex cube, so reachability ranges from NP-complete to undecidable depending on the time bound; at width 6, robust verification is NP-complete for tanh, sigmoid, GELU and other smooth activations.

papers.title: Joint Certification for Attributed Graphs: Beyond Topology-Only Robustness
Learning Better Certified Models from Empirically-Robust Teachers
papers.summary: Improves certified training of ReLU networks through feature-space knowledge distillation from adversarially trained teachers, significantly raising the performance of existing certified training algorithms on robust computer vision benchmarks while keeping models amenable to verification.

papers.title: Learning Provable Neural Network Observer for Uncertain Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: Trains neural network state observers with certified Lyapunov stability in two stages, point-guided Lyapunov pre-training on sampled states followed by LMI fine-tuning for a global certificate; it trains much faster than direct LMI methods and tracks better on nonlinear control benchmarks and X-29 aircraft.

papers.title: Learning Reach-Set Geometry for Tighter Probabilistic Neural Network Verification
Multi-Constrained Randomized Smoothing Certificates
Pareto DNN Verification: Fast for Most Queries
papers.summary: PAVE adds early exits to DNNs and verifies robustness exit by exit, solving roughly 80% of queries in a fraction of the time of direct verification; break and continue optimizations cut SAFE-case time up to 10x, enabling verification of ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100.

papers.title: Provable Robustness against Backdoor Attacks via the Primal-Dual Perspective on Differential Privacy
papers.summary: Certifies robustness to backdoor attacks, which perturb training and test data jointly, by linking randomized smoothing to differential-privacy privacy profiles that compose training- and inference-time mechanisms; instantiated for DP-SGD and Deep Partition Aggregation and evaluated on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

papers.title: Provably Safe, Yet Scalable Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: PS2-RL learns provably safe RL policies without explicitly computing invariant sets: a learned backup policy forward-integrates the dynamics to form an implicit control-invariant set, and a differentiable projection layer enforces safety during policy training; evaluated on robotic tasks with up to 10 state dimensions.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
papers.summary: Certifies safety of unknown monotone dynamical systems from simulator queries with monotone neural barrier certificates built from Max-Monotone Networks, reducing checks to finitely many boundary cells and O(n) queries; it scales to oscillator networks with 13,659 states and traffic networks with 1,000 states.

papers.title: Should We Pay This Much for Robustness? Efficient Proxy Certificates with Marginal Guarantees
papers.summary: Replaces costly randomized smoothing certificates with a cheap proxy tuned by robust conformal risk control to bound the marginal false-approval rate; standalone it needs one forward pass per input, and as a fallback it recovers randomized smoothing's certified ratio, extending to vision transformers and language models.

papers.title: Sparse Sum-of-Squares Layers for Certified Learning
papers.summary: Sparse SOS Layers make sum-of-squares certificates differentiable within learning pipelines by reusing the sparse forward solve in the backward pass, giving up to 2.7x faster warm calls and roughly 100x less memory; a design study reaches zero certified violations on unseen instances.

papers.title: Towards Sound Verification of Deployed Neural Networks
Verifying Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: RSB uses actor-critic reinforcement learning to refine branching heuristics in branch-and-bound DNN verifiers, rescaling baseline neuron scores with attention over neuron features and graph embeddings; on 600 challenging instances it solves 11% more and explores 50% fewer branches.

papers.title: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness for Automatic Speech Recognition
papers.summary: Applies a certification-inspired pipeline to automatic speech recognition: a Two-Sided Atomic Audit statistically certifies token existence and adversarial exclusion, and a Rank-Based Tournament selects the output sequence; across four architectures, Word Error Rate drops by up to 55% relative.

months.label: June 2026
months.intro: ECCV 2026 and IROS 2026 decisions: vision-focused verification, with IoUCert for anchor-based object detectors, robustness certificates for semantic segmentation and a local Lipschitz bound for Transformers, plus post-training reachability verification of safety-constrained RL policies for robot navigation.

papers.title: Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning with Post-Training Reachability Verification for Robot Navigation
papers.summary: Trains robot navigation policies with CVaR-constrained TD3, then checks them by computing action reachable sets under bounded observation noise with Taylor Models; across ten scenarios it reaches 98.3% success and the highest safety verification rate, and transfers to a physical Jackal robot.

papers.title: Fast and Flexible Robustness Certificates for Semantic Segmentation
IoUCert: Robustness Verification for Anchor-Based Object Detectors
Pay Attention to Attention Distribution: A New Local Lipschitz Bound for Transformers

months.label: May 2026
months.intro: ICFP 2026 decisions: the Vehicle framework is extended so neural network specifications transpile to interactive theorem provers such as Rocq, Isabelle/HOL, Agda and Imandra, giving infinite time-horizon safety proofs for neural-controlled cyber-physical systems.

papers.title: Compositional Neural-Cyber-Physical System Verification in the Interactive Theorem Prover of Your Choice
papers.summary: Extends the Vehicle framework so neural network specifications transpile to any interactive theorem prover, integrating Rocq, Isabelle/HOL, Agda and Imandra; this yields infinite time-horizon safety proofs for neural-controlled cyber-physical systems, including a continuous medical device verified in Rocq.

months.label: April 2026
months.intro: CAV 2026, ICML 2026, IJCAI 2026, ISSTA 2026 and RSS 2026 decisions: randomized smoothing and probabilistic certificates lead, including certified model ownership with CREDIT and Cert-LAS. Verification tooling grows toward theorem provers with Rocq-NN-Roll and VNN-LIB 2.0 in Agda, while transformers, segmentation networks and quantised networks get dedicated analyses; formal explanations cover Verified SHAP, Certified Circuits and GNN semifactuals.

papers.title: ARQ: A Mixed-Precision Quantization Framework for Accurate and Certifiably Robust DNNs
papers.summary: ARQ searches mixed-precision quantizations of DNNs with reinforcement learning while keeping the clean accuracy and certified robustness of randomized-smoothing classifiers; quantized networks match floating-point models using only 1.5% of instructions and reach the highest certified radius.

papers.title: ATKVerifier: Adaptive Top-K Constraints for Tighter Verification of Semantic Segmentation Networks
papers.summary: Verifies semantic segmentation networks with a constrained-star abstract domain that adds adaptive top-K lower bounds and affine upper bounds for MaxPool; on M2NIST it improves robust IoU by 8-25% over the ImageStar-based NNV baseline and certifies 35.2% more complete objects on a 24-layer network.

papers.title: Perception with Guarantees: Certified Pose Estimation via Reachability Analysis
papers.summary: Certifies 3D pose estimation from a single camera image and a known target geometry by formally bounding the pose with reachability analysis and neural network verification; experiments show efficient, accurate localization in both synthetic and real-world settings.

papers.title: Precise Verification of Transformers Through ReLU-Catalyzed Abstraction Refinement
papers.summary: Verifies transformers more precisely by expressing self-attention dot products as ReLU-based non-linear bounds, then reusing ReLU convex relaxations in rule-based and optimization-based frameworks; on sentiment-analysis robustness properties it improves precision over the baseline at an acceptable efficiency cost.

papers.title: QAV-FT: Quadratic Approximation-Based Neural Network Verification via Fourier Series and Taylor Truncation
papers.summary: QAV-FT verifies networks with high-frequency activations such as Swish, GELU and Mish using Fourier-based quadratic abstractions and second-order propagation with Taylor remainder error control, reaching an average certification accuracy of 96.8% on MNIST-FC and other benchmarks.

papers.title: The Rocq-NN-Roll Prover: Soundly Verifying Hyperproperties of Neural Networks in Rocq
papers.summary: Rocq-NN-Roll is a formally verified prover, built in Rocq, for rational-valued piecewise-affine neural networks that checks properties including hyperproperties by reducing them to linear inequalities over polyhedral regions, giving the first automated network proof support in an interactive theorem prover.

papers.title: VNN-LIB 2.0: Rigorous Foundations for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Gives VNN-LIB 2.0 formal foundations: a network theory that abstracts the semantics needed from model formats such as ONNX, plus a more expressive query language with formal syntax, type system and semantics, all mechanised in the Agda theorem prover.

papers.title: Parallel Differentiable Reachability for Learning and Planning with Certified Neural Dynamics and Controllers
papers.summary: A parallel, differentiable reachability framework in JAX combines Taylor-model flowpipes with CROWN-style bound propagation for closed-loop neural dynamics and controllers, enabling certified training and reachability-aware MPC; demonstrated on manipulation and quadrotor tasks up to 72 dimensions, including hardware.

papers.title: ExLipBaB: Exact Lipschitz Constant Computation for Piecewise Linear Neural Networks
papers.summary: ExLipBaB generalizes the LipBaB algorithm to compute exact Lipschitz constants of arbitrary continuous piecewise linear networks under p-norms, covering ReLU, LeakyReLU, GroupSort, MaxMin, FullSort and MaxPool, for uses such as benchmarking approximations and robustness guarantees for small models.

papers.title: Leveraging Over-Parameterization to Improve the Verifiability of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Shows that over-parameterization can reduce neuron instability, a key factor in verification cost, so wider networks can become easier to verify; experiments suggest it may help reconcile the long-standing trade-off between generalization and verifiability of neural networks.

papers.title: Lookahead Branching for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Adds lookahead branching to branch-and-bound neural network verifiers, framing the FSB heuristic as a special case and deriving extra lemmas that speed up search; implemented in Marabou and α-β-CROWN, it gives consistent speedups and up to 57% more solved instances.

papers.title: Probabilistic Verification of Recurrent Neural Networks for Single and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: RNN-ProVe estimates the probability of undesired behavior in recurrent RL policies by sampling the hidden states feasible under the trained policy and attaching statistical error bounds, giving high-confidence guarantees in partially observable single-agent and cooperative multi-agent tasks.

papers.title: Semifactual Explanations for GNN-based Classification: Formal Foundations, Complexity and Computation
papers.summary: Studies semifactual explanations for GNN classifiers, the maximal subgraph perturbations that leave a prediction unchanged; analyzes the computational complexity of related reasoning and optimization problems and proposes a learning architecture that computes high-quality semifactuals.

papers.title: Synthesis and Verification of Transformer Programs
papers.summary: Verifies C-RASP transformer programs by reducing them to Lustre synchronous dataflow programs checked with SMT-based model checkers, and learns C-RASPs from examples via local search; demonstrated on transformer program minimization and constrained learning from partial specifications.

papers.title: The Complexity of Verifying Feedforward Neural Networks in Quantised Settings
papers.summary: Maps the complexity of verifying feedforward networks with rational, quantised and dynamically quantised weights under linear-programming and bit-vector specifications: fixed-precision quantised verification is NP-complete for both, and upper bounds are given for dynamically quantised networks with bit-vector specifications.

papers.title: CREDIT: Certified Ownership Verification of Deep Neural Networks Against Model Extraction Attacks
papers.summary: CREDIT certifies ownership of DNNs against model extraction attacks by measuring model similarity with mutual information and setting a verification threshold backed by theoretical guarantees; evaluated on several mainstream datasets across domains and tasks.

papers.title: Cert-LAS: Toward Certified Model Ownership Verification for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Layer-Adaptive Smoothing
papers.summary: Cert-LAS certifies ownership of text-to-image diffusion models by embedding watermarks with diffusion classifiers and layer-adaptive noise, then hypothesis-testing watermark responses against unwatermarked references; it is proven reliable under removal attacks under certain conditions and resists adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Certified Circuits: Stability Guarantees for Mechanistic Circuits
papers.summary: Certified Circuits wrap any circuit discovery method with randomized data subsampling to certify that component inclusion is stable under bounded edits to the concept dataset; on ResNet, ViT and GPT-2, circuits reach up to 56% higher accuracy with up to 80% fewer components.

papers.title: Certified Robustness under Heterogeneous Perturbations via Hybrid Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Extends randomized smoothing to joint perturbations of discrete and continuous inputs via a Neyman–Pearson analysis, giving a closed-form one-dimensional certificate that generalizes both Gaussian and discrete smoothing; applied to multimodal text–image safety filtering.

papers.title: Certifying Graph Neural Networks Against Label and Structure Poisoning
papers.summary: ST-GPA certifies graph neural networks against node-label and graph-structure poisoning by enriching graph partitions with pseudo-labels and synthetic edges in a partition-and-aggregate scheme, significantly improving certificates across benchmarks while keeping strong clean accuracy.

papers.title: Does a Hybrid Space-Aware Randomized Defense Improve Empirical and Certified Adversarial Robustness?
papers.summary: HySCAN combines random weights and stochastic attention noise injection at training and inference to give ℓ2 certified guarantees and stronger empirical ℓ∞ robustness, improving certified robustness by up to about 9.6% and empirical robustness by up to about 5% without reducing clean accuracy.

papers.title: Front-Loaded Robust Conformal Prediction: Heavy Calibration, Minimal Test-Time Cost
papers.summary: Front-Loaded robust conformal prediction shifts randomized smoothing samples to calibration while using one or very few samples at test time, matching the test-time cost of existing methods while producing considerably smaller prediction sets at larger radii.

papers.title: Higher-Order Certified Robustness for Regression
papers.summary: Certifies regression models under randomized smoothing with a prediction-centered certificate built from means, variances and gradients of the smoothed model; on an MNIST rotation task, using gradient information gives significantly tighter certificates than α-smoothing.

papers.title: Neural Vector Lyapunov–Razumikhin Certificates for Delayed Interconnected Systems
papers.summary: Learns and verifies neural vector Lyapunov–Razumikhin certificates for scalable input-to-state stability of discrete-time interconnected systems with communication delays; on mixed-autonomy platoons, drone formations and microgrids it verifies more efficiently with competitive control performance.

papers.title: Probabilistic Robustness Certificates against Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: Models stochastic gradient training as a dynamical system and uses neural barrier certificates with PAC guarantees from a scenario convex program to probabilistically certify the largest robust ℓp radius; model-agnostic and evaluated on MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR-10.

papers.title: Rethinking Evaluation Paradigms in IBP-based Certified Training
papers.summary: Re-evaluates IBP-based certified training by comparing Pareto fronts of natural versus certified accuracy found with automated multi-objective hyperparameter tuning, exposing undertuned prior configurations, setting new best results and showing earlier advances were smaller than assumed.

papers.title: Semantic Robustness Certification for Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Certifies vision-language model predictions under semantic transformations such as shape, size and style, using text prompts as proxies and a closed-form decision boundary to certify ranges of transformation extent without extra data for each variation.

papers.title: Verified SHAP: Provable Bounds for Exact Shapley Values of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Uses neural network verification to compute arbitrarily tight lower and upper bounds on exact SHAP values of neural networks, eventually recovering the exact values, and scales to search spaces orders of magnitude larger than existing exact methods.

months.label: March 2026
months.intro: PLDI 2026 and S&P 2026 decisions: SAIL uses LLMs to synthesize sound abstract transformers for neural network verification, and EnCP gives conformal prediction certified robustness against data poisoning.

papers.title: SAIL: Sound Abstract Interpreters with LLMs
papers.summary: Sail uses LLMs to synthesize globally sound abstract transformers for neural network verification, guided by a cost function measuring unsoundness plus syntactic and semantic validation; it matches hand-designed transformers and produces sound, precise ones for complex non-linear operators absent from the literature.

papers.title: Ensemble Conformal Predictor (EnCP): A New Conformal Predictor with Robustness Guarantees Against Data Poisoning Attacks
papers.summary: EnCP is an ensemble-based conformal predictor with provable robustness to data poisoning, bounding the influence of poisoned samples to derive certified coverage and certified prediction-set size; on image classification and LLM toxicity classification it keeps high coverage and compact sets under attack.

months.label: February 2026
months.intro: CVPR 2026 decisions: verification beyond ℓp perturbations, with Lipschitz optimization bounding homography-transformed pixels under 3D camera motion and robustness verification under dual perturbations.

papers.title: Lipschitz Optimization for Formal Verification of Homographies
papers.summary: Verifies vision networks against 3D camera-motion perturbations by mapping camera pose to pixels and using Lipschitz optimization to bound homography-transformed pixel values; reports up to 89% speed-up and 7% tighter bounds than prior work, and exposes weaknesses in VNN-COMP benchmarks and a runway classifier.

papers.title: Verifying Neural Network Robustness with Dual Perturbations

months.label: January 2026
months.intro: ICLR 2026 and ICRA 2026 decisions: formal explanations lead, with FAME, verified circuit discovery, explanations for Neural Additive Models and a complexity-theoretic unification. Theory covers multi-neuron convex relaxations and the parameterized hardness of zonotope containment, while certification scales up through LipNeXt, dual randomized smoothing and probabilistic verification of the full YOLO pipeline; ICRA adds safety verification of generative motion planners.

papers.title: Certified vs. Empirical Adversarial Robustness via Hybrid Convolutions with Attention Stochasticity
papers.summary: HyCAS couples 1-Lipschitz spectrally normalized convolutions with random projection filters and attention noise, yielding a randomized network that is at most 2-Lipschitz with L2 certificates; it raises certified accuracy by up to 7.3% and empirical robustness by up to 3.1% on imaging benchmarks.

papers.title: Certifying the Full YOLO Pipeline: A Probabilistic Verification Approach
papers.summary: Probabilistically verifies YOLO object detectors against object disappearance by estimating output ranges under input perturbation distributions, formally verifying non-maximum suppression within them, and refining iteratively; it gives comparable guarantees and tighter IoU lower bounds with far fewer samples than existing methods.

papers.title: Dual Randomized Smoothing: Beyond Global Noise Variance
papers.summary: Dual randomized smoothing certifies robustness with input-dependent noise variances, proven valid when locally constant, using a separately smoothed variance estimator feeding a standard smoothed classifier; on CIFAR-10 it beats prior input-dependent methods by up to 20.0% at 60% inference overhead.

papers.title: EnsembleSHAP: Faithful and Certifiably Robust Attribution for Random Subspace Method
papers.summary: EnsembleSHAP is a feature attribution method for the random subspace method that reuses its computational byproducts, stays efficient, keeps properties such as local accuracy, and is provably robust to explanation-preserving attacks; evaluated against backdoor, adversarial and jailbreak attacks.

papers.title: Expressiveness of Multi-Neuron Convex Relaxations in Neural Network Certification
papers.summary: Analyzes the expressiveness of multi-neuron convex relaxations for ReLU network certification, proving them inherently incomplete (a universal convex barrier), while showing completeness is reachable by adding polynomially many ReLU neurons or by partitioning the input into convex sub-polytopes.

papers.title: FAME: Formal Abstract Minimal Explanation for Neural Networks
papers.summary: FAME computes formal abductive explanations for neural networks via abstract interpretation, progressively shrinking dedicated perturbation domains and using LiRPA bounds to discard irrelevant features; against VERIX+ it gives smaller explanations and lower runtime on medium- to large-scale networks.

papers.title: Formal Mechanistic Interpretability: Automated Circuit Discovery with Provable Guarantees
papers.summary: Uses neural network verification to discover circuits with provable guarantees of input-domain robustness, robust patching and minimality, and links the three theoretically; experiments with verifiers on vision models yield circuits with substantially stronger robustness guarantees than standard circuit discovery.

papers.title: How Catastrophic is Your LLM? Certifying Risks in Conversation
LipNeXt: Scaling up Lipschitz-based Certified Robustness to Billion-parameter Models
papers.summary: LipNeXt is a constraint-free, convolution-free 1-Lipschitz architecture trained by manifold optimization on the orthogonal manifold with a Spatial Shift Module; it scales Lipschitz-based certification to 1-2B-parameter ImageNet models, improving certified robust accuracy by up to 8% at ε=1.

papers.title: Out of the Shadows: Exploring a Latent Space for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Refines inputs for neural network verification by transferring output specifications back through the latent space of zonotope set propagation, shrinking the input set to unsafe regions; the GPU-friendly, matrix-only tool cuts branch-and-bound subproblems and competes with top VNN-COMP tools.

papers.title: Parameterized Hardness of Zonotope Containment and Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Proves parameterized hardness for ReLU network verification: deciding positivity of an ℓ-layer network is W[ℓ−1]-hard in the input dimension, so zonotope non-containment is W[1]-hard; maximum and Lipschitz-constant approximation are also hard, making naive enumeration essentially optimal under the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

papers.title: Provably Explaining Neural Additive Models
papers.summary: Generates provably cardinally-minimal sufficient explanations for Neural Additive Models using only logarithmically many verification queries in the number of features after parallel preprocessing; yields smaller explanations and much lower runtime than existing algorithms for the weaker subset-minimal variant.

papers.title: Unifying Formal Explanations: A Complexity-Theoretic Perspective
papers.summary: Unifies sufficient and contrastive explanations as minimizing one probabilistic value function whose complexity depends on monotonicity, submodularity and supermodularity; global settings admit polynomial-time algorithms for neural networks, decision trees and tree ensembles, while local versions remain NP-hard.

papers.title: Formal Safety Verification and Refinement for Generative Motion Planners via Certified Local Stabilization
papers.summary: Certifies closed-loop safety of generative motion planners by stabilizing sampled references with a small neural tracking controller and applying neural network verification to obtain reachable sets; verified references are reused online, improving safety for diffusion, flow-matching and vision-language planners in simulation and hardware.

months.label: December 2025
months.intro: FSE 2026 and OOPSLA 2026 decisions: complete ReLU verification with fewer binary variables through SART, precondition synthesis with statistical guarantees via StatPre, and structural robustness verification of DNNs with VeriS.

papers.title: SART: Sign-Absolute Reformulation Theory for Binary Variable Reduction in Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: SART cuts the binary variables needed for complete ReLU network verification below one per unstable neuron, proving final-layer variables can be halved; the LayerABS verifier extends the gain to all layers through progressive tightening and outperforms existing baselines across benchmarks.

papers.title: Precondition Synthesis for Deep Neural Networks with Statistical Guarantees
papers.summary: Synthesizes preconditions for deep neural networks with statistical guarantees via StatPre, a select-and-solve framework using Box-based abstraction, cluster-based center selection and statistical model approximation; on 15 models and 27 properties from 6 benchmarks it gives broader coverage than 4 existing schemes.

papers.title: Verifying Structural Robustness of Deep Neural Network
papers.summary: Verifies structural robustness of DNNs against coordinated linear position-invariant and position-varying perturbations; VeriS encodes these perturbations as subnetworks so existing local-robustness verifiers apply, verifying 78% of 5508 problems across image, audio and healthcare networks.

months.label: November 2025
months.intro: AAAI 2026 decisions: neural control safety leads, with ReLU barrier certificate verification and falsification, LUCID and probabilistic policy verification via predicate abstraction. Formal explanations get faster with VeriX+ and abductive latent explanations for prototype networks, while abstract domains target transformer self-attention and RNNs with DeepPrism; Lipschitz estimation goes quantum-classical with HiQ-Lip.

papers.title: CertMask: Certifiable Defense Against Adversarial Patches via Theoretically Optimal Mask Coverage
papers.summary: CertMask certifies image classifiers against adversarial patches with a single round of masking whose mask set covers every patch location at least k times, cutting cost from O(n^2) to O(n); it raises certified robust accuracy by up to 13.4% over PatchCleanser.

papers.title: Certified L2-Norm Robustness of 3D Point Cloud Recognition in the Frequency Domain
papers.summary: FreqCert certifies 3D point cloud classifiers against global l2 perturbations by applying the graph Fourier transform, voting over spectrally partitioned sub-point clouds, and deriving a tight closed-form certified radius; it achieves higher certified accuracy on ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN.

papers.title: Efficient Verification and Falsification of ReLU Neural Barrier Certificates
papers.summary: States a necessary and sufficient condition for the correctness of ReLU neural barrier certificates for continuous-time systems, encodable as SMT or optimization, enabling both verification and, for the first time, falsification; numerical experiments confirm its validity and effectiveness.

papers.title: Efficiently Computing Compact Formal Explanations
papers.summary: VeriX+ shrinks and speeds up formal explanations for ML models using bound-propagation-based sensitivity, binary-search traversal with confidence ranking and an adapted QuickXplain; it cuts explanation size by 38% on GTSRB and time by 90% on MNIST, scaling to transformers.

papers.title: Formal Abductive Latent Explanations for Prototype-Based Networks
papers.summary: Abductive Latent Explanations give sufficient conditions on the latent representation of prototype-based case-based reasoning networks that imply the prediction, addressing misleading prototype explanations; a solver-free, scalable algorithm generates them for standard and fine-grained image classification.

papers.title: HiQ-Lip: A Hierarchical Quantum-Classical Method for Global Lipschitz Constant Estimation of ReLU Networks
papers.summary: HiQ-Lip estimates global Lipschitz constants of ReLU networks with a hybrid quantum-classical method, casting the problem as Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization with multilevel graph coarsening; on two-layer networks with 256 hidden neurons it doubles solving speed and gives tighter upper bounds than LiPopt.

papers.title: LUCID: Learning-Enabled Uncertainty-Aware Certification of Stochastic Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: LUCID certifies safety of black-box stochastic dynamical systems from transition data by learning control barrier certificates in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space with ambiguity sets, using a finite Fourier kernel expansion to turn a semi-infinite non-convex problem into a linear program.

papers.title: Learning Vision-Based Neural Network Controllers with Semi-Probabilistic Safety Guarantees
papers.summary: Verifies and trains vision-based neural network controllers in a semi-probabilistic framework combining reachability analysis, conditional generative networks and distribution-free tail bounds, with a safety loss and curriculum learning; evaluated in X-Plane 11, CARLA, a physical F1Tenth setup and AirSim.

papers.title: On the Probabilistic Learnability of Compact Neural Network Preimage Bounds
papers.summary: RF-ProVe approximates neural network preimages probabilistically, using an ensemble of randomized decision trees to propose input regions satisfying an output property and refining them by active resampling, with formal statistical guarantees on region purity and global coverage.

papers.title: Parameterized Abstract Interpretation for Transformer Verification
papers.summary: Proposes two parameterized linear abstract domains for inner products in transformer self-attention, one from symbolic quadratic bounds and tangents, one interpolating prior affine bounds; both verify robustness instances existing methods cannot and give tighter interval results, especially in deeper networks.

papers.title: Probabilistic Safety Verification of Neural Policies via Predicate Abstraction
papers.summary: Extends policy predicate abstraction to probabilistic safety verification of neural action policies, adapting probabilistic CEGAR to neural policies; the algorithm decides whether a policy meets an unsafety-probability bound and derives upper and lower bounds where encodings into probabilistic model checkers prove ineffective.

papers.title: Tighter Truncated Rectangular Prism Approximation for RNN Robustness Verification
papers.summary: DeepPrism verifies RNN robustness by enclosing the Hadamard-product surface with a truncated rectangular prism of two linear planes, refined to minimize volume and surface area; it improves on existing approaches in image classification, speech recognition and sentiment analysis tasks.

papers.title: VeriFlow: Modeling Distributions for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: VeriFlow is a flow-based density model with a piecewise-affine transformation, letting linear-arithmetic verifiers restrict global properties such as fairness or robustness to a data distribution, since upper density level sets become linear constraints in the latent space.

months.label: September 2025
months.intro: NeurIPS 2025 decisions: probabilistic certification leads, spanning AdaptDel for edit-distance robustness, robust conformal prediction from one sample and certified safe LLM generation with C-SafeGen. Bound propagation speeds up through Clip-and-Verify, neural control work certifies Lyapunov stability of RL policies and controllers, and MIBP-Cert certifies training against data perturbations; DNN verification proofs and provable gradient editing also appear.

papers.title: Abstract Rendering: Certified Rendering Under 3D Semantic Uncertainty
AdaptDel: Adaptable Deletion Rate Randomized Smoothing for Certified Robustness
papers.summary: Certifies sequence classifiers against edit-distance perturbations with AdaptDel, which extends randomized smoothing to deletion rates that adapt to input properties such as length; on natural language tasks the median certified region cardinality improves by up to 30 orders of magnitude.

papers.title: C-SafeGen: Certified Safe LLM Generation with Claim-Based Streaming Guardrails
papers.summary: Provides certified safety for LLM generation through Claim-based Stream Decoding, which guards sequential claims with a streaming guardrail model and backtracks on risky ones; conformal analysis yields a high-probability upper bound on safety risk that can be controlled to any desired level asymptotically.

papers.title: Certifying Stability of Reinforcement Learning Policies using Generalized Lyapunov Functions
papers.summary: Certifies stability of reinforcement learning policies by learning generalized Lyapunov functions that augment RL value functions with neural residual terms and only require decrease on average over multiple steps; certifies Gymnasium and DeepMind Control policies and enlarges certified regions of attraction.

papers.title: Clip-and-Verify: Linear Constraint-Driven Domain Clipping for Accelerating Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Speeds up branch-and-bound neural network verification with Clip-and-Verify, which uses linear constraints from bound propagation to clip verified or irrelevant input regions and tighten intermediate bounds on GPU; integrated into α,β-CROWN, it cuts subproblems by up to 96%.

papers.title: Compositional Neural Network Verification via Assume-Guarantee Reasoning
Fortifying Time Series: DTW-Certified Robust Anomaly Detection
papers.summary: Certifies time-series anomaly detectors against perturbations bounded in Dynamic Time Warping distance by adapting randomized smoothing and linking ℓp-norm certificates to DTW through a lower-bound transformation; F1-score under DTW-based attacks improves by up to 18.7% over traditional certified models.

papers.title: Generating and Checking DNN Verification Proofs
MIBP-Cert: Certified Training against Data Perturbations with Mixed-Integer Bilinear Programs
papers.summary: Certifies training against data errors, corruptions and poisoning with MIBP-Cert, which computes the set of parameters reachable from perturbed data via mixed-integer bilinear programming and a sound per-step relaxation, giving deterministic robustness bounds for continuous and discrete data under complex threat models.

papers.title: One Sample is Enough to Make Conformal Prediction Robust
papers.summary: Makes conformal prediction robust to bounded input noise with a single forward pass on a randomly perturbed input, certifying the conformal procedure itself via any binary certificate; RCP1 yields smaller average robust sets than methods using around 100 passes per input.

papers.title: Probabilistic Stability Guarantees for Feature Attributions
papers.summary: Certifies the stability of feature attributions with soft stability and a model-agnostic, sample-efficient stability certification algorithm (SCA) for any attribution method; Boolean function analysis explains why mild smoothing gives a better accuracy-stability trade-off, with evaluation on vision and language tasks.

papers.title: Provable Gradient Editing of Deep Neural Networks
ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
papers.summary: Gives provable robustness for RAG-based web search against retrieval-corpus corruption with ReliabilityRAG, which finds a reliability-weighted Maximum Independent Set on a document contradiction graph to filter malicious documents, plus a scalable weighted sample-and-aggregate variant that keeps some guarantees.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Network Geometric Robustness Validation via Hölder Optimisation
Scaling Data-Driven Probabilistic Robustness Analysis for Semantic Segmentation Neural Networks
Sound Logical Explanations for Mean Aggregation Graph Neural Networks
papers.summary: Characterizes the monotonic logical rules that can be sound for mean-aggregation graph neural networks with non-negative weights (MAGNNs) and gives a first-order logic fragment that explains any MAGNN prediction; restricting weights keeps comparable or better accuracy on inductive knowledge graph benchmarks.

papers.title: Two‑Stage Learning of Stabilizing Neural Controllers via Zubov Sampling and Iterative Domain Expansion
papers.summary: Jointly trains and verifies neural controllers and Lyapunov functions for continuous-time systems using Zubov-inspired sampling and domain expansion, extending α,β-CROWN to bound propagation through system Jacobians; regions of attraction grow 5 to 150,000 times and verification runs 40 to 10,000 times faster than dReal.

months.label: August 2025
months.intro: ASE 2025 decisions: harder verification benchmarks from ReluSplitter, which destabilizes neurons while preserving semantics, and provable fairness repair of DNNs with PROF.

papers.title: Destabilizing Neurons to Generate Challenging Neural Network Verification Benchmarks
papers.summary: Generates harder neural network verification benchmarks with ReluSplitter, which destabilizes stable neurons in existing benchmarks through semantics-preserving transformations so the ground truth is unchanged; the resulting instances substantially raise difficulty for current DNN verifiers while keeping verifiable answers.

papers.title: Provable Fairness Repair for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Repairs individual-fairness violations in DNNs with PROF, which uses interval bound propagation to bound outputs over the set around a biased sample and solves a MILP for model modifications; repaired models generalize to up to 95.93% of full datasets and 93.16% of the input space.

months.label: July 2025
months.intro: CCS 2025 decisions: provable repair of DNN defects from backdoor, adversarial and safety-property threats with ProRepair, via preimage synthesis and property refinement.

papers.title: Provable Repair of Deep Neural Network Defects by Preimage Synthesis and Property Refinement
papers.summary: Repairs DNN defects from backdoor, adversarial and safety-property threats with ProRepair, which synthesizes proxy boxes for feature-space preimages and refines properties; it is 5x to 2000x faster than prior provable point-wise repair and fixes all 36 safety violations versus 8.

months.label: June 2025
months.intro: OOPSLA 2025 and IROS 2025 decisions: tighter activation convex hull approximation with WraAct, mini-batch robustness verification with BaVerLy, and quantization guaranteed to match floating-point classifications with CoMPAQt. Certified individual fairness through training and the feasibility of real-time randomized smoothing certification round out the month.

papers.title: Convex Hull Approximation for Activation Functions
papers.summary: Builds tight over-approximations of activation function convex hulls with WraAct, which smooths functions using double-linear-piece functions; versus SBLM+PDDM it is on average 400X faster and 150X more precise, and within a verifier it beats PRIMA by up to 20 verified samples.

papers.title: Correct-by-Construction: Certified Individual Fairness through Neural Network Training
papers.summary: Guarantees individual fairness throughout neural network training via provably fair initialization and a fairness-preserving training algorithm using randomized response mechanisms to protect sensitive attributes; resulting models are fair and accurate, and training is much faster than certified training that runs verification.

papers.title: Mini-Batch Robustness Verification of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Verifies local robustness of many ϵ-balls jointly with BaVerLy, a sound and complete verifier that groups balls with similar network computations into adaptively sized mini-batches and refines on failure; on MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks it is 2.3x faster on average, up to 4.1x.

papers.title: Quantization with Guaranteed Floating-Point Neural Network Classifications
papers.summary: Guarantees quantized networks match floating-point classifications using CoMPAQt, a MILP encoding with custom relaxations that bounds the confidence of inconsistent inputs and drives correction mechanisms; one guarantees 100% consistency while cutting computational cost 3.8x on average, another reaches near-perfect consistency at 4.1x.

papers.title: Feasibility Analysis of real-time Robustness Certification
papers.summary: Studies how cutting the number of randomized smoothing samples by orders of magnitude affects certified radius, finding only modest loss in average certified radius that off-the-shelf improvements can offset, enabling real-time robustness certification on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

months.label: May 2025
months.intro: ICML 2025 decisions: probabilistic certification leads, from a critique of average certified radius to cost-sensitive smoothing and branch-and-bound for probabilistic verification. Certified training is re-examined with CTBench and BRONet, SDP-CROWN brings SDP tightness to bound propagation, and formal explanations use abstraction-refinement; floating-point soundness of deployed verifiers is also questioned.

papers.title: Average Certified Radius is a Poor Metric for Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Argues average certified radius is a flawed metric for randomized smoothing, proving trivial classifiers can reach arbitrarily large ACR and that it overweights easy samples; strategies exploiting this reach top ACR on CIFAR-10, and the distribution of p_A is proposed instead.

papers.title: Beyond Topological Self-Explainable GNNs: A Formal Explainability Perspective
papers.summary: Formalizes the minimal explanations of self-explainable GNNs and compares them to prime implicant and faithful explanations, finding they match PI explanations only for some tasks; proposes Dual-Channel GNNs combining a white-box rule extractor with an SE-GNN that recover succinct rules.

papers.title: CTBench: A Library and Benchmark for Certified Training
papers.summary: Introduces CTBench, a library and benchmark that evaluates deterministic certified training algorithms under fair schedules, certification and tuned hyperparameters; most algorithms beat their reported results, recent gains shrink against tuned baselines, and certified models show sparser activations and shared mistakes.

papers.title: Certification for Differentially Private Prediction in Gradient-Based Training
papers.summary: Improves differentially private prediction by computing dataset-specific upper bounds on prediction sensitivity with convex relaxation and bound propagation, combined with the smooth sensitivity mechanism; on medical imaging and NLP data these bounds can be orders of magnitude tighter than global sensitivity.

papers.title: Efficient Robust Conformal Prediction via Lipschitz-Bounded Networks
papers.summary: Estimates robust conformal prediction sets with lip-rcp using Lipschitz-bounded networks, giving smaller sets and faster computation than prior robust CP on medium and large tasks such as ImageNet, and derives worst-case coverage bounds for vanilla CP valid across all attack levels.

papers.title: Enhancing Certified Robustness via Block Reflector Orthogonal Layers and Logit Annealing Loss
papers.summary: Improves certified robustness of Lipschitz networks with a Block Reflector Orthogonal (BRO) layer and a logit annealing loss that raises margins for most points; the resulting BRONet outperforms baselines on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet.

papers.title: Exact Upper and Lower Bounds for the Output Distribution of Neural Networks with Random Inputs
papers.summary: Computes guaranteed upper and lower bounds on the output CDF of neural networks with random inputs by bounding general networks with ReLU networks; bounds converge to the true CDF as resolution grows and cover CNNs and feedforward networks with activations like ReLU, tanh and softmax.

papers.title: Explaining, Fast and Slow: Abstraction and Refinement of Provable Explanations
papers.summary: Computes provably sufficient explanations of neural network predictions faster through abstraction-refinement: a reduced network whose sufficient explanations also hold for the original speeds verification, and the network is gradually enlarged when an explanation fails, giving interpretations across abstraction levels.

papers.title: LEVIS: Large Exact Verifiable Input Spaces for Neural Networks
papers.summary: Finds large verifiable input regions free of adversarial examples with LEVIS: LEVIS-α computes one large verifiable ball and LEVIS-β covers the space with multiple balls, using mixed-integer programming plus complementarity-constrained optimization for up to 6 times faster runtime.

papers.title: No Soundness in the Real World: On the Challenges of the Verification of Deployed Neural Networks
papers.summary: Shows that current neural network verifiers are not practically sound, since bounding full-precision outputs does not bound floating-point outputs in deployment; adversarial networks exploiting floating-point operation order and precision fool every tested verifier, and practical soundness is argued to be computationally harder.

papers.title: Pixel-level Certified Explanations via Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Certifies pixel-level robustness of any black-box attribution method against ℓ2-bounded perturbations by sparsifying and smoothing attribution maps with randomized smoothing, treated as segmentation; evaluating 12 attribution methods on 5 ImageNet models shows the certified attributions are robust, interpretable and faithful.

papers.title: Probably Approximately Global Robustness Certification
papers.summary: Certifies a probabilistic relaxation of global robustness by sampling an ε-net and querying a local robustness oracle, with sample size independent of input dimension, class count and learning algorithm; it scales beyond formal methods and characterizes robustness better than sampling approaches.

papers.title: Provably Cost-Sensitive Adversarial Defense via Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Certifies and trains for cost-sensitive robustness, where misclassification harms are given by a cost matrix, by defining a cost-sensitive certified radius and adapting randomized smoothing certification, plus a training method that improves this robustness without hurting accuracy.

papers.title: SDP-CROWN: Efficient Bound Propagation for Neural Network Verification with Tightness of Semidefinite Programming
papers.summary: Combines SDP tightness with bound-propagation scalability in SDP-CROWN, adding a linear bound that captures ℓ2-norm inter-neuron coupling with one extra parameter per layer, up to √n tighter than per-neuron bounds; inside α-CROWN it verifies models with 65 thousand neurons.

papers.title: Solving Probabilistic Verification Problems of Neural Networks using Branch and Bound
papers.summary: Solves probabilistic verification problems, such as demographic parity fairness, by iteratively refining lower and upper output-probability bounds with bound propagation and branch and bound; it cuts solve times from tens of minutes to tens of seconds and is sound, and complete under mild conditions.

months.label: April 2025
months.intro: CAV 2025, IJCAI 2025 and USENIX Security 2025 decisions: verification tools lead, with NeuralSAT, StarV, ModelVerification.jl and a Dafny-verified robustness certifier. Neural control work brings logarithmic neural certificates, deductive RL synthesis and KAN controllers with barrier certificates; theory covers floating-point universal approximation and PSPACE-completeness for quantized GNNs, alongside space explanations and FaVeR fairness repair.

papers.title: A Formally Verified Robustness Certifier for Neural Networks
papers.summary: Implements and formally verifies in Dafny a certification function for globally-robust neural networks, after showing previous unverified implementations can be exploitably unsound and that approximations like power iteration do not guarantee soundness; describes specifications, design decisions and practical experience.

papers.title: Deductive Synthesis of Reinforcement Learning Agents for Infinite Horizon Tasks
papers.summary: Synthesizes reinforcement learning agents that provably satisfy infinite-horizon temporal reach-avoid specifications by decomposing them into finite-horizon subtasks with separate policies, using formal verification to guarantee the composition; synthesized agents beat standard RL in performance and specification compliance.

papers.title: Floating-Point Neural Networks are Provably Robust Universal Approximators
papers.summary: Proves the first interval universal approximation theorem for floating-point neural networks, showing their interval abstract semantics can exactly capture the direct image map of any rounded target function; corollaries include existence of provably robust floating-point networks and a computational completeness result.

papers.title: ModelVerification.jl: A Comprehensive Toolbox for Formally Verifying Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Presents ModelVerification.jl, a toolbox collecting a suite of methods for formally verifying different types of DNNs against varied input-output specifications, aimed at giving developers and practitioners a single self-contained verification framework.

papers.title: NeuralSAT: A High-Performance Verification Tool for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Presents the latest version of NeuralSAT, a DNN verification tool based on the DPLL(T) framework that supports many architectures and activation functions; after a New Participant Award and 4th place at VNN-COMP'23, it placed second at VNN-COMP'24.

papers.title: Policy Verification in Stochastic Dynamical Systems Using Logarithmic Neural Certificates
papers.summary: Verifies neural network policies in discrete-time stochastic systems against reach-avoid specifications using learned neural certificates, introducing logarithmic reach-avoid supermartingales and weighted-norm Lipschitz bounds to shrink Lipschitz constants; it verifies specifications with probabilities as high as 99.9999%.

papers.title: Space Explanations of Neural Network Classification
papers.summary: Introduces space explanations, logic-based explanations of neural network classification that give provable guarantees over continuous input regions, generated with Craig interpolation and unsatisfiable cores; case studies of various sizes show them more meaningful than existing explanations.

papers.title: StarV: A Qualitative and Quantitative Verification Tool for Learning-Enabled Systems
papers.summary: Presents StarV, a star-reachability tool for verifying DNNs and learning-enabled cyber-physical systems, adding ProbStar reachability and ProbStar Temporal Logic for quantitative verification and a SparseImageStar representation for memory-efficient CNN and segmentation verification; it beats existing tools in speed, scalability and memory.

papers.title: Efficient Counterexample-Guided Fairness Verification and Repair of Neural Networks Using Satisfiability Modulo Convex Programming
papers.summary: Verifies and repairs individual fairness in pre-trained neural networks with FaVeR, which uses counterexamples from satisfiability modulo convex programming to locate high-sensitivity neurons and adjust their weights; it repairs 100% of models with under 2.27% accuracy loss.

papers.title: Efficient and Rigorous Model-Agnostic Explanations
papers.summary: Proposes efficient algorithms for symbolic, model-agnostic explanations that explain samples of a black-box model's behavior, keeping the rigor of logic-based explainability without needing access to model internals; experiments confirm the algorithms scale.

papers.title: Formal Synthesis of Safe Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Controllers with Barrier Certificates
papers.summary: Synthesizes safe controllers and control barrier certificates using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks instead of feed-forward networks, then prunes and symbolizes them so candidates can be formally verified with Satisfiability Modulo Theories; the KAN4CBC tool handles higher system dimensions with better efficiency.

papers.title: GraphProt: Certified Black-Box Shielding Against Backdoored Graph Models
papers.summary: Shields GNN graph classifiers against backdoor attacks with GraphProt, a certified black-box defense that filters topology and features, samples subgraphs, and takes a majority vote over subgraph predictions; it lowers attack success rates while preserving clean classification accuracy.

papers.title: Neuron Similarity-Based Neural Network Verification via Abstraction and Refinement
papers.summary: Speeds up DNN verification with ARVerifier, which merges similar neurons based on interval outputs into a smaller abstract network and refines on spurious counterexamples; on ACAS Xu and MNIST it cuts verification time by 11.61%, 18.70% and 12.20% for α,β-CROWN, Verinet and Marabou.

papers.title: Verifying Quantized Graph Neural Networks is PSPACE-complete
papers.summary: Shows that verifying quantized graph neural networks through the linear-constrained validity problem (LVP) is PSPACE-complete for reasonable activation functions, via a translation into a logical language, a proof system, and a matching hardness proof.

papers.title: CertTA: Certified Robustness Made Practical for Learning-Based Traffic Analysis

months.label: March 2025
months.intro: S&P 2025 decisions: FairZK proves fairness of logistic regression and deep neural network models in zero-knowledge while keeping parameters secret.

papers.title: FairZK: A Scalable System to Prove Machine Learning Fairness in Zero-Knowledge
papers.summary: Proves fairness of logistic regression and deep neural network models in zero-knowledge, keeping parameters secret, by bounding fairness from parameters and aggregated input information plus dedicated proof protocols. FairZK speeds up proving 3.1x-1789x and handles a 47-million-parameter model in 343 seconds.

months.label: February 2025
months.intro: CVPR 2025 decisions: certification of human trajectory prediction, deterministic GNN certification against graph poisoning with PGNNCert, PatchDEMUX for multi-label patch defense, and tighter MaxPool verification with Ti-Lin.

papers.title: Certified Human Trajectory Prediction
papers.summary: Certifies human trajectory prediction models against noisy or adversarial inputs, addressing unbounded and multi-modal outputs, with a diffusion-based trajectory denoiser to limit performance loss and new certified performance metrics; certified predictors show accuracy and robustness advantages over non-certified ones.

papers.title: Deterministic Certification of Graph Neural Networks against Graph Poisoning Attacks with Arbitrary Perturbations
papers.summary: Certifies GNNs against training-time poisoning with PGNNCert, giving deterministic guarantees under arbitrary edge, node and node-feature perturbations for node and graph classification; it significantly outperforms prior certified defenses limited to edge or node perturbations.

papers.title: PatchDEMUX: A Certifiably Robust Framework for Multi-label Classifiers Against Adversarial Patches
papers.summary: Extends single-label certifiable patch defenses to multi-label classifiers with PatchDEMUX, treating the task as isolated binary problems, plus a tighter procedure for single-patch attackers; with PatchCleanser as backbone it achieves non-trivial robustness on MS-COCO and PASCAL VOC with high clean performance.

papers.title: Tightening Robustness Verification of MaxPool-based Neural Networks via Minimizing the Over-Approximation Zone
papers.summary: Tightens robustness verification of MaxPool-based CNNs with Ti-Lin, giving provably neuron-wise tightest linear bounds for MaxPool; across LeNet, PointNet and networks on MNIST, CIFAR-10, Tiny ImageNet and ModelNet40 it improves certified accuracy by up to 78.6% at similar runtime.

months.label: January 2025
months.intro: ICLR 2025 and ICRA 2025 decisions: probabilistic certification leads, with robust conformal prediction, Fuzzed Randomized Smoothing against backdoors and certified uncertainty calibration. Language models get certificates for counterfactual bias and domain, poisoning defenses cover GNN labels and offline RL, and theory addresses transformer encoder satisfiability; ICRA adds NeuralPARC for reach-avoid through narrow gaps.

papers.title: Certified Robustness Under Bounded Levenshtein Distance
papers.summary: Certifies text classifiers under Levenshtein distance with LipsLev, which computes Lipschitz constants of convolutional classifiers with respect to Levenshtein distance to train 1-Lipschitz models certified in one forward pass; it reaches 38.80% and 13.93% verified accuracy on AG-News, 4 orders of magnitude faster.

papers.title: Certifying Counterfactual Bias in LLMs
papers.summary: Certifies LLMs for counterfactual bias with LLMCert-B, producing high-confidence bounds on the probability of unbiased responses for prompts differing in demographic group, drawn from prefix distributions such as random tokens and jailbreak mixtures; non-trivial certificates expose vulnerabilities in leading LLMs.

papers.title: Certifying Language Model Robustness with Fuzzed Randomized Smoothing: An Efficient Defense Against Backdoor Attacks
papers.summary: Certifies pre-trained language models against backdoor attacks with Fuzzed Randomized Smoothing (FRS), combining biphased parameter smoothing with Monte Carlo tree search fuzzing to find vulnerable text segments in Damerau-Levenshtein space, without needing poisoned data; it gives a broader certified radius than prior methods.

papers.title: Exact Certification of (Graph) Neural Networks Against Label Poisoning
papers.summary: Certifies GNNs exactly against label-flipping poisoning by using the Neural Tangent Kernel to rewrite the bilevel problem as a MILP, giving sample-wise and collective certificates; it ranks GNN architectures and reveals robustness plateaus at intermediate perturbation budgets.

papers.title: Multi-level Certified Defense Against Poisoning Attacks in Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Certifies offline reinforcement learning against data poisoning at both per-state action and cumulative reward levels using differential privacy properties, across continuous, discrete, stochastic and deterministic settings; performance drops at most 50% with up to 7% poisoned data, with 5 times larger certified radii.

papers.title: Provably Reliable Conformal Prediction Sets in the Presence of Data Poisoning
papers.summary: Builds conformal prediction sets with provable reliability under training and calibration poisoning through reliable prediction sets (RPS), using smoothed scores aggregated over classifiers trained on data partitions and majority votes over sets calibrated on distinct subsets; validated on image classification.

papers.title: Provably Robust Explainable Graph Neural Networks against Graph Perturbation Attacks
papers.summary: Proposes XGNNCert, a provably robust explainable GNN that guarantees explanations under worst-case graph perturbations with a bounded number of perturbed edges stay close to unattacked ones without affecting GNN predictions; evaluated across several graph datasets and GNN explainers.

papers.title: Robust Conformal Prediction with a Single Binary Certificate
papers.summary: Makes conformal prediction robust to adversarial inputs by binarizing smoothed samples with a coverage-preserving threshold, needing only one binary certificate instead of certifying each point; it yields smaller robust sets with far fewer Monte Carlo samples, such as 150 for CIFAR10, and drops bounded-score requirements.

papers.title: Robust Representation Consistency Model via Contrastive Denoising
papers.summary: Improves randomized smoothing with a consistency model that turns diffusion denoising into latent-space contrastive instance discrimination, enabling single-pass denoise-then-classify; on ImageNet it beats diffusion-based certified accuracy by 5.3% on average, up to 11.6%, with 85 times lower inference cost.

papers.title: Shh, don't say that! Domain Certification in LLMs
Support is All You Need for Certified VAE Training
papers.summary: Trains variational autoencoders with certified probabilistic guarantees under adversarial attacks using CIVET, which bounds worst-case VAE error through error on chosen support sets in the latent layer; it outperforms prior methods across wireless and vision datasets, architectures and perturbation sizes.

papers.title: Towards Certification of Uncertainty Calibration under Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: Certifies uncertainty calibration of neural classifiers under adversarial perturbations, giving analytic worst-case bounds on the Brier score and mixed-integer-program bounds on expected calibration error, and introduces calibration attacks used for adversarial calibration training.

papers.title: Towards a Unified and Verified Understanding of Group-Operation Networks
papers.summary: Reverse-engineers one-hidden-layer networks trained on finite group operations and verifies the explanation by turning it into a compact proof of model performance; for symmetric group S5 models it runs 3x faster than brute force and gives at least 95% accuracy bounds for 45% of models.

papers.title: Transformer Encoder Satisfiability: Complexity and Impact on Formal Reasoning
papers.summary: Analyzes the complexity of transformer encoder satisfiability (trSAT), relevant to formal verification, showing it undecidable for commonly studied encoders but decidable for quantized ones, where it is NEXPTIME-hard in some scenarios and in NEXPTIME in others.

papers.title: Verifying Properties of Binary Neural Networks Using Sparse Polynomial Optimization
papers.summary: Verifies robustness of Binary Neural Networks against ℓ∞ and ℓ2 attacks with semidefinite programming relaxations from sparse polynomial optimization, an alternative to SMT and MILP that supports continuous inputs, avoids floating-point issues, and improves scalability through tighter first-order relaxations.

papers.title: Guaranteed Reach-Avoid for Black-Box Systems through Narrow Gaps via Neural Network Reachability
papers.summary: NeuralPARC extends PARC reach-avoid computation to ReLU networks trained on robot trajectory data, computing reachable sets with modeling error to return states and parameters that guarantee a black-box system reaches its goal through narrow gaps, shown on drift parking and a surface vehicle.

months.label: December 2024
months.intro: AAAI 2025, OOPSLA 2025 and USENIX Security 2025 decisions: neural network control systems lead, with barrier certificates from Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, verified multi-agent path finding and certificate repair via runtime monitoring. Randomized smoothing certifies sensor fusion and speaker recognition, while OOPSLA work covers soundness of DNN certifiers (ProveSound), incremental verification (Olive) and bit-flip attacks on quantized neural networks (BFAVerifier).

papers.title: COMMIT: Certifying Robustness of Multi-Sensor Fusion Systems Against Semantic Attacks
papers.summary: COMMIT certifies multi-sensor fusion perception in autonomous vehicles against semantic transformations such as rotation and shifting, using anisotropic randomized smoothing on multi-modal data with grid-based splitting; on CARLA, fusion models certify up to 48.39% higher than single-modal ones.

papers.title: Certification of Speaker Recognition Models to Additive Perturbations
papers.summary: Certifies speaker recognition models against norm-bounded additive perturbations by transferring and improving randomized smoothing certification from images to audio, for both classification and few-shot settings, with evaluation of several models on VoxCeleb 1 and 2.

papers.title: Certified Causal Defense with Generalizable Robustness
papers.summary: GLEAN is a certified defense that adds certifiable causal factor learning to separate causal from spurious features, then certifies robustness against attacks on latent causal factors, so that certified robustness carries over to domains with distribution shift on benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Formal Synthesis of Barrier Certificates Using Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
papers.summary: Synthesizes barrier certificates for cyber-physical systems with Fourier Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks instead of feed-forward networks, then formally checks candidates with a Lipschitz method and Satisfiability Modulo Theories; the KAN4BC tool improves verification efficiency and success rate on benchmarks.

papers.title: Learning Verified Safe Neural Network Controllers for Multi-Agent Path Finding
papers.summary: VSMANC jointly trains decentralized control barrier functions and neural controllers for multi-agent path finding, with a formal verification-guided retraining loop that checks the barrier functions and feeds counterexamples back, giving verified safety in shape formation and UAV simulations.

papers.title: Neural Control and Certificate Repair via Runtime Monitoring
papers.summary: Certifies and repairs neural control policies and their certificate functions, such as barrier or Lyapunov functions, when system dynamics are unknown, using runtime monitoring that detects violations and turns them into retraining data; raises safety rates on two control tasks.

papers.title: PROSAC: Provably Safe Certification for Machine Learning Models under Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: PROSAC certifies that a model's adversarial population risk stays below a threshold through a calibration-based hypothesis test with Bayesian optimization over attacks; applied to ViT and ResNet models, it finds ViTs and larger models generally more robust.

papers.title: Probabilistic Shielding for Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Gives safe reinforcement learning strict formal guarantees when the MDP safety dynamics are known and safety is an undiscounted probabilistic avoidance property, by augmenting the MDP state and shielding the agent's actions; the agent stays safe in both training and testing.

papers.title: Scalable Surrogate Verification of Image-Based Neural Network Control Systems Using Composition and Unrolling
papers.summary: Verifies image-based neural network control systems with a cGAN surrogate by composing dynamics, generator and controller into one network and unrolling several control steps, so existing verifiers yield tighter reachable sets; the prior baseline's set is 175% larger on aircraft taxiing.

papers.title: Sparse Transfer Learning Accelerates and Enhances Certified Robustness: A Comprehensive Study
papers.summary: Speeds up L2-norm certified robustness verification on downstream tasks by reusing pre-training verification results with sparse updates, dynamic sparse mask selection and a stability regularizer called DiffStab, cutting verification time by up to 70-80% with slight certified accuracy loss.

papers.title: Training Verification-Friendly Neural Networks via Neuron Behavior Consistency
papers.summary: Trains verification-friendly networks by keeping neuron activation states consistent within a local input neighborhood, reducing unstable neurons and tightening bounds; on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 the networks stay verifiable at larger radii where other tools fail.

papers.title: AGNNCert: Defending Graph Neural Networks against Arbitrary Perturbations with Deterministic Certification
papers.summary: Certifies GNNs against arbitrary combined edge, node and node-feature perturbations with AGNNCert, giving deterministic guarantees for both node and graph classification and covering earlier certified defenses as special cases; it also outperforms prior defenses on edge-only and node-only perturbations.

papers.title: CAMP in the Odyssey: Provably Robust Reinforcement Learning with Certified Radius Maximization
papers.summary: Trains certifiably robust deep RL policies with CAMP, which optimizes a surrogate loss tied to local certified radii under policy smoothing and stabilizes training through policy imitation; it achieves up to twice the certified expected return of baselines.

papers.title: CertPHash: Towards Certified Perceptual Hashing via Robust Training
Automated Verification of Soundness of DNN Certifiers
papers.summary: Automatically verifies the soundness of abstract-interpretation-based DNN certifiers written in the ConstraintFlow DSL with ProveSound, which introduces symbolic DNNs to reduce soundness over arbitrary architectures to a tractable form checkable by standard SMT solvers, covering both existing and new certifiers.

papers.title: Efficient Incremental Verification of Neural Networks Guided by Counterexample Potentiality
papers.summary: Accelerates incremental verification of a modified network with Olive, which reuses a branch-and-bound template from a similar network and orders subproblems by counterexample potentiality, in greedy and balanced variants; on 1445 MNIST and CIFAR-10 instances it beats classic and incremental verifiers, especially on falsifiable ones.

papers.title: Guarding the Privacy of Label-Only Access to Neural Network Classifiers via iDP Verification
papers.summary: Provides individual differential privacy for label-only access to classifiers with LUCID, which computes an iDP deterministic bound using MILP encoding, hyper-network abstraction, branch-and-bound and linear relaxation, adding noise only where needed; perfect 0-iDP costs 1.4% accuracy versus 12.7% for DP training.

papers.title: Verification of Bit-Flip Attacks against Quantized Neural Networks
papers.summary: Formally verifies resilience of quantized neural networks to bit-flip attacks, or finds all vulnerable parameters, with BFAVerifier, combining reachability analysis over symbolic parameters in a new abstract domain with an equivalent MILP encoding when abstraction fails, making it sound and complete.

months.label: November 2024
months.intro: ICSE 2025 decisions: fairness certification and repair. Fairquant certifies and quantifies individual fairness of deep neural networks via symbolic interval analysis, and Patchpro repairs local robustness by attaching patch modules guided by formal verification.

papers.title: Fairquant: Certifying and Quantifying Fairness of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Certifies and quantifies individual fairness of deep neural networks by abstracting symbolic interval analysis and refining it guided by the fairness property, reporting the percentage of provably fair individuals; on four fairness datasets it is more accurate and orders of magnitude faster than prior techniques.

papers.title: Patch Synthesis for Property Repair of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Patchpro repairs local robustness of DNNs by attaching patch modules that fix all samples in a robustness neighborhood, using formal verification and a heuristic patch allocation; it achieves provable property-level repair in 100% of cases across several high-dimensional datasets.

months.label: September 2024
months.intro: NeurIPS 2024 decisions: randomized smoothing leads, extended to multi-step defences, regression models, Deep Equilibrium Models and diffusion purification. Safe control is the other strand, with Dynamic Model Predictive Shielding, VerSAILLE's differential dynamic logic and SEEV's ReLU barrier functions, while BICCOS adds cutting planes to branch-and-bound and RABBit targets relational verification.

papers.title: Achieving Domain-Independent Certified Robustness via Knowledge Continuity
Adaptive Randomized Smoothing: Certified Adversarial Robustness for Multi-Step Defences
papers.summary: Adaptive Randomized Smoothing certifies test-time adaptive, multi-step image classifiers against L-infinity adversarial examples by analyzing randomized smoothing with f-Differential Privacy; it improves standard accuracy by 1 to 15 points and ImageNet certified accuracy by up to 1.6 points.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized α-Smoothing for Regression Models
Certified Robustness for Deep Equilibrium Models via Serialized Random Smoothing
papers.summary: Brings randomized smoothing certification to Deep Equilibrium Models, with Serialized Randomized Smoothing reusing historical information to cut redundant computation and a new certified radius estimate; certification of DEQs runs up to 7x faster with almost no loss in certified accuracy.

papers.title: Consistency Purification: Effective and Efficient Diffusion Purification towards Certified Robustness
papers.summary: Consistency Purification improves diffusion-based purification for randomized smoothing by using a one-step consistency model, fine-tuned with an LPIPS loss, to keep purified images on the data manifold and semantically aligned, giving better certified robustness and efficiency than baselines.

papers.title: Diffusion Models are Certifiably Robust Classifiers
Dynamic Model Predictive Shielding for Provably Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Dynamic Model Predictive Shielding keeps reinforcement learning provably safe during and after training by using a local planner, informed by the neural policy's reward estimates, to choose recovery actions; recovery regret falls exponentially with planning depth and rewards exceed baselines.

papers.title: ECLipsE: Efficient Compositional Lipschitz Constant Estimation for Deep Neural Networks
