papers.summary: ECLipsE estimates Lipschitz constants of deep feed-forward networks compositionally, splitting the large matrix verification problem into per-layer subproblems solved by small SDPs or in closed form; it runs up to thousands of times faster with bounds close to or better than prior methods.

papers.title: FedGMark: Certifiably Robust Watermarking for Federated Graph Learning
On the Scalability of Certified Adversarial Robustness with Generated Data
Provable Editing of Deep Neural Networks using Parametric Linear Relaxation
Provably Safe Neural Network Controllers via Differential Dynamic Logic
papers.summary: VerSAILLE derives neural network specifications from differential dynamic logic control envelopes so that a network proof yields infinite-time safety of the closed loop; Mosaic verifies the resulting polynomial arithmetic properties on piecewise-linear networks, proving safety on airborne collision avoidance benchmarks.

papers.title: Relational Verification Leaps Forward with RABBit
SEEV: Synthesis with Efficient Exact Verification for ReLU Neural Barrier Functions
papers.summary: SEEV synthesizes ReLU neural control barrier functions with a regularizer that reduces activation regions on the safety boundary, and verifies them exactly using tight over-approximations of the safety conditions per linear segment, improving verification efficiency while keeping barrier function quality.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Network Verification with Branch-and-bound Inferred Cutting Planes
papers.summary: BICCOS strengthens branch-and-bound neural network verification with cutting planes inferred from neuron relationships in verified subproblems, plus influence-based strengthening and multi-tree search; it verifies more instances than other verifiers, scales to large networks and is part of α,β-CROWN.

papers.title: Treatment of Statistical Estimation Problems in Randomized Smoothing for Adversarial Robustness
papers.summary: Examines statistical estimation in randomized smoothing certification, giving confidence-sequence procedures with optimal sample complexity and the same guarantees as standard methods for deciding robustness at a radius, plus a randomized Clopper-Pearson interval that yields strictly stronger certificates.

papers.title: Verifiably Robust Conformal Prediction
papers.summary: VRCP restores conformal prediction coverage under adversarial attacks using neural network verification instead of randomized smoothing, supporting l1, l2 and l-infinity perturbations and regression; on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet and deep RL tasks it keeps above-nominal coverage with tighter prediction regions.

papers.title: Verified Safe Reinforcement Learning for Neural Network Dynamic Models
papers.summary: Learns control policies for nonlinear neural network dynamical systems that are verified safe via finite-horizon reachability, using a curriculum that lengthens the verified horizon, incremental verification and multiple initial-state-dependent controllers; verified horizons are up to an order of magnitude longer than baselines.

months.label: July 2024
months.intro: CCS 2024, ECCV 2024 and ISSTA 2024 decisions: vision-focused certification, including certifiably robust image watermarks and face recognition, cross-input certified training for universal perturbations and ProTIP for text-to-image diffusion models. Certified continual learning for neural network regression and a certified defense against backdoors in federated graph learning complete the picture.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustification via Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Certifiably Robust Image Watermark
Cross-Input Certified Training for Universal Perturbations
ProTIP: Probabilistic Robustness Verification on Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Against Stochastic Perturbation
Towards Certifiably Robust Face Recognition
Certified Continual Learning for Neural Network Regression
papers.summary: Certified continual learning keeps the verified correctness properties of a neural network intact for as long as possible while it is retrained on new data, extending existing continual learning methods; across several networks, trained models keep their certified correctness and usually high utility.

papers.title: Distributed Backdoor Attacks on Federated Graph Learning and Certified Defenses
papers.summary: Proposes a subgraph-trigger backdoor attack on federated graph learning and a certified defense that splits test graphs into subgraphs and takes a majority vote, giving deterministic, provably tight robustness against triggers of any shape and location across six graph datasets.

months.label: June 2024
months.intro: IROS 2024 decisions: neural network repair for robotic safety, fixing behavioral-cloning robot policies to satisfy safety constraints given predictive models, shown on mobile robot navigation and lower-leg prostheses.

papers.title: Repairing Neural Networks for Safety in Robotic Systems using Predictive Models
papers.summary: Repairs robot policies learned by behavioral cloning so they satisfy safety constraints, applying neural network repair subject to predictive models of quantities such as proprioceptive states or collision likelihood; demonstrated on mobile robot navigation and real lower-leg prostheses.

months.label: May 2024
months.intro: ICML 2024 and RSS 2024 decisions: randomized smoothing and conformal prediction lead, from hierarchical segmentation certification and smoothed DRL agents to C-RAG for retrieval-augmented language models. Other directions include ∂-CROWN for physics-informed neural networks, relational verification with RACoon, Lyapunov-stable neural control, and POLICEd RL for robot policies with hard constraints.

papers.title: Adaptive Hierarchical Certification for Segmentation using Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Certifies semantic segmentation with randomized smoothing over a class hierarchy, relaxing unstable pixels to coarser classes instead of abstaining, and introduces the Certified Information Gain metric; on Cityscapes, PASCAL-Context, ACDC and COCO-Stuff it lowers abstain rate and raises CIG.

papers.title: Breaking the Barrier: Enhanced Utility and Robustness in Smoothed DRL Agents
papers.summary: S-DQN and S-PPO train randomized-smoothing DRL agents with better clean reward, empirical robustness and robustness guarantees, beating existing smoothed agents by 2.16x and robustly trained agents by 2.13x on average under the strongest attack; a stronger Smoothed Attack is also introduced.

papers.title: C-RAG: Certified Generation Risks for Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
papers.summary: C-RAG certifies generation risks of retrieval-augmented language models through conformal risk analysis, giving an upper confidence bound that also holds under distribution shift, and proves RAG attains lower conformal generation risk than a single LLM given non-trivial retrieval quality.

papers.title: Certifiably Byzantine-Robust Federated Conformal Prediction
papers.summary: Rob-FCP makes federated conformal prediction robust to Byzantine clients reporting arbitrary statistics, with a proven coverage bound asymptotically near the target and an estimator for an unknown number of malicious clients, evaluated on five benchmark and healthcare datasets.

papers.title: Collective Certified Robustness against Graph Injection Attacks
papers.summary: Certifies a set of target nodes in graph neural networks at once against graph injection attacks by formulating a binary integer quadratic constrained program and relaxing it to a linear program; on Citeseer the certified ratio rises from 0.0% to 81.2%.

papers.title: Compositional Curvature Bounds for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Bounds the second derivative of continuously differentiable deep networks layer by layer, using the curvature bound with local gradients to give robustness and attack certificates and as a differentiable training regularizer; evaluated on MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification.

papers.title: Effects of Exponential Gaussian Distribution on (Double Sampling) Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Studies Exponential Standard Gaussian and Exponential General Gaussian smoothing distributions for randomized smoothing and Double Sampling Randomized Smoothing, deriving certified radius formulas and tighter l2 lower bounds; EGG raises DSRS certified accuracy by up to 6.4% on ImageNet.

papers.title: Efficient Error Certification for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.summary: ∂-CROWN certifies the worst-case residual error of physics-informed neural networks over their whole continuous domain after training, giving tight certificates for PINNs solving Burgers', Schrödinger's, Allan-Cahn and Diffusion-Sorption equations.

papers.title: FairProof : Confidential and Certifiable Fairness for Neural Networks
papers.summary: FairProof publicly verifies the fairness of a confidential fully-connected neural network with zero-knowledge proofs, using a fairness certification algorithm designed to suit such proofs; it is implemented in Gnark and shown to be practically feasible.

papers.title: Fine-grained Local Sensitivity Analysis of Standard Dot-Product Self-Attention
papers.summary: LoFAST analyzes the local sensitivity of dot-product self-attention to l2 input perturbations, showing it is controlled by the attention weight matrices and the unperturbed input, and yields non-vacuous certified l2 robustness for vision transformers on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.

papers.title: Local vs. Global Interpretability: A Computational Complexity Perspective
papers.summary: Uses computational complexity to compare local and global explanations for linear models, decision trees and neural networks, proving that finding global sufficient subsets is harder than local ones for linear models, while the reverse holds for neural networks and decision trees.

papers.title: Lyapunov-stable Neural Control for State and Output Feedback: A Novel Formulation
papers.summary: Learns neural network controllers and observers with Lyapunov certificates over a larger verifiable region of attraction, using fast falsification in training and post-hoc branch-and-bound with linear bound propagation instead of SOS, MIP or SMT solvers; gives formally stable output feedback control.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Policy Iteration: Algorithms, Convergence, and Verification
papers.summary: Proposes extreme learning machine and physics-informed neural network variants of policy iteration for nonlinear optimal control with convergence guarantees, outperforming Galerkin methods, and applies formal verification to show the resulting controllers are stable.

papers.title: Relational DNN Verification With Cross Executional Bound Refinement
papers.summary: RACoon verifies relational properties of DNNs, such as robustness to universal adversarial perturbations and worst-case hamming distance, by exploiting cross-execution dependencies at every layer, gaining substantial precision over existing baselines across datasets, networks and properties.

papers.title: Robust Yet Efficient Conformal Prediction Sets
papers.summary: Makes conformal prediction sets provably robust to evasion and calibration poisoning by bounding the worst-case change in conformity scores; tighter bounds give smaller sets, covering continuous and sparse discrete data and attacks on both features and labels.

papers.title: VNN: Verification-Friendly Neural Networks with Hard Robustness Guarantees
Verifying message-passing neural networks via topology-based bounds tightening
papers.summary: Certifies robustness of ReLU message-passing neural networks with mixed-integer optimization, handling edge addition and removal, global and local budgets and feature changes, and tightening bounds using graph topology; implemented as an extension of the SCIP branch-and-cut solver.

papers.title: POLICEd RL: Learning Closed-Loop Robot Control Policies with Provable Satisfaction of Hard Constraints
papers.summary: POLICEd RL learns robot control policies that provably satisfy affine hard state constraints with a black-box environment by making the policy affine around the unsafe set as a repulsive buffer; it works with any RL training algorithm and outperforms existing methods.

months.label: April 2024
months.intro: IJCAI 2024 decisions: verification of parameterised neural-symbolic multi-agent systems against a bounded CTL fragment, and Truth Table Net, convolutional networks that convert into compact CNF Boolean circuits for fast exact robustness verification.

papers.title: Formal Verification of Parameterised Neural-symbolic Multi-agent Systems
papers.summary: Verifies multi-agent systems with arbitrarily many agents, each with a neural network perception unit and programmed action selection, against a bounded CTL fragment, using an abstraction that reduces the problem to Neural Interpreted Systems with a bounded number of agents.

papers.title: Truth Table Net: Scalable, Compact & Verifiable Neural Networks with a Dual Convolutional Small Boolean Circuit Networks Form
papers.summary: TTnet builds convolutional networks from Learning Truth Table filters that convert exactly into compact CNF Boolean circuits, making formal verification fast; it reaches 41% ImageNet accuracy and performs exact robustness verification in 10ms versus 100s for traditional DNN solvers.

months.label: March 2024
months.intro: CAV 2024 and S&P 2024 decisions: tools and control stand out, with Marabou 2.0, VELM's reachability-based safe exploration and neural barrier certificates for DNN-controlled systems. Other directions are few-pixel verification via covering designs, global two-safety properties, a Bayes-error bound on certified robust accuracy, and certified defenses for few-shot classification (FCert) and graph injection attacks.

papers.title: FCert: Certifiably Robust Few-Shot Classification in the Era of Foundation Models
papers.summary: FCert is a certified defense against data poisoning of few-shot classifiers built on foundation models, provably keeping the predicted label when the number of poisoned support samples is bounded; it outperforms existing certified poisoning defenses on vision and text benchmarks.

papers.title: Node-aware Bi-smoothing: Certified Robustness against Graph Injection Attacks
papers.summary: Node-aware bi-smoothing certifies node classification against graph injection attacks with a model-agnostic smoothing scheme covering both evasion and poisoning; it derives certifiable conditions, extends two existing certification frameworks to node injection for comparison, and is also applied to recommendation systems.

papers.title: Boosting Few-Pixel Robustness Verification via Covering Verification Designs
papers.summary: Speeds up L0 few-pixel robustness verification with covering verification designs, choosing among candidate coverings by predicting their block size distribution in closed form and building them on the fly in parallel; verification time drops by up to 5.1x on average.

papers.title: Certified Robust Accuracy of Neural Networks Are Bounded Due to Bayes Errors
papers.summary: Derives an upper bound on certified robust accuracy from Bayes error under data distribution uncertainty, explaining why certified training lowers accuracy; for CIFAR10 the bound is 67.49%, while existing methods reached 62.84% by 2023.

papers.title: Marabou 2.0: A Versatile Formal Analyzer of Neural Networks
papers.summary: System description of version 2.0 of Marabou, a framework for formal analysis of neural networks, covering its architectural design and the main features and components added since the first release.

papers.title: Safe Exploration in Reinforcement Learning by Reachability Analysis over Learned Models
papers.summary: VELM keeps reinforcement learning exploration safe by learning symbolic environment models, running formal reachability analysis on them, and shielding the agent to states verified safe; it cuts safety violations compared with other safe learning methods without lowering reward.

papers.title: Unifying Qualitative and Quantitative Safety Verification of DNN-Controlled Systems
papers.summary: Verifies DNN-controlled systems by synthesizing neural barrier certificates, first for almost-sure safety and, if that fails, for lower and upper bounds on probabilistic safety over finite and infinite horizons, using k-inductive certificates and simulation-guided training on four systems.

papers.title: Verifying Global Two-Safety Properties in Neural Networks with Confidence
papers.summary: Verifies confidence-based 2-safety properties of DNNs, such as global robustness and global fairness, by self-composition with a new verifiable abstraction of softmax, proven sound and implemented on top of Marabou with evaluation on public benchmarks.

months.label: February 2024
months.intro: CVPR 2024, PLDI 2024 and USENIX Security 2024 decisions: certified defenses for vision, including PatchCURE against adversarial patches, MMCert for multi-modal models, median randomized smoothing for super-resolution and a comparison of 1-Lipschitz layers. MaxLin tightens linear approximation for MaxPool-based CNNs, and RaVeN verifies input-relational properties with the DiffPoly domain.

papers.title: PatchCURE: Improving Certifiable Robustness, Model Utility, and Computation Efficiency of Adversarial Patch Defenses
papers.summary: PatchCURE is a tunable framework of certified defenses against adversarial patches that trades off certifiable robustness, utility and computation; at efficiency close to undefended models it gains 16-23% absolute clean and certified robust accuracy over prior defenses.

papers.title: 1-Lipschitz Layers Compared: Memory, Speed, and Certifiable Robustness
papers.summary: Compares 1-Lipschitz layer methods for certifiably robust networks on computational complexity, memory, time per epoch, accuracy and certified robust accuracy, and gives guidelines for choosing a method based on the available resources.

papers.title: MMCert: Provable Defense Against Adversarial Attacks to Multi-Modal Models
papers.summary: MMCert is a certified defense for multi-modal models that lower-bounds performance under bounded perturbations to every modality, such as changed pixels in RGB and depth images; on road segmentation and emotion recognition it beats a certified defense extended from unimodal models.

papers.title: Towards General Robustness Verification of MaxPool-Based Convolutional Neural Networks via Tightening Linear Approximation
papers.summary: MaxLin verifies robustness of MaxPool-based CNNs by tightening the linear approximation of MaxPool to certify larger lower bounds; on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet networks it improves the certified bound by up to 110.60% with up to 5.13x speedup.

papers.title: Universal Robustness via Median Randomized Smoothing for Real-World Super-Resolution
papers.summary: Compares robustness methods for real-world image super-resolution and finds median randomized smoothing generalizes across adversarial attacks better than adversarial training, while also helping SR models handle blur, Gaussian noise and natural real-world corruptions.

papers.title: Input-Relational Verification of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: RaVeN verifies input-relational DNN properties such as universal adversarial perturbation robustness and monotonicity with DiffPoly, an abstract domain tracking output differences between executions at every layer, combined with linear programming; it is substantially more precise than baselines.

months.label: January 2024
months.intro: ICLR 2024 and FSE 2024 decisions: randomized smoothing and certified training lead, with conformal prediction certificates (COLEP, RSCP+), dual and incremental smoothing, and studies of IBP certified training and expressive losses. SDP-based Lipschitz estimation recurs, and FSE adds VeriStable for DPLL-based verification and CrossCert for patch robustness certification.

papers.title: A Recipe for Improved Certifiable Robustness
papers.summary: Improves Lipschitz-based deterministic certification by exploring the design space, adding large Cholesky-orthogonalized residual dense layers to Lipschitz-controlled ResNets and filtered generative data augmentation, raising the best deterministic VRA by up to 8.5 percentage points.

papers.title: COLEP: Certifiably Robust Learning-Reasoning Conformal Prediction via Probabilistic Circuits
papers.summary: COLEP certifies the coverage of conformal prediction under bounded adversarial perturbations by combining learned semantic models with reasoning via probabilistic circuits; certified coverage improves by up to 12% on GTSRB, 9% on CIFAR-10 and 14% on AwA2.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness for Rate Encoded Spiking Neural Networks
papers.summary: Gives the first provable l1-norm robustness guarantee for rate-encoded spiking neural networks by linking rate encoding to randomized smoothing, and adds adversarial training that improves empirical robust accuracy on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100.

papers.title: DRSM: De-Randomized Smoothing on Malware Classifier Providing Certified Robustness
papers.summary: DRSM certifies malware detectors against contiguous adversarial bytes by adapting de-randomized smoothing to MalConv with a window ablation scheme, at a marginal accuracy cost, and releases PACE, a public dataset of 15.5K benign executables.

papers.title: Expressive Losses for Verified Robustness via Convex Combinations
papers.summary: Argues that loss expressivity, spanning lower and upper bounds of the worst-case loss through one coefficient, is key to verified training, showing simple convex combinations of adversarial attacks and IBP bounds reach state-of-the-art verified robustness across settings.

papers.title: Expressivity of ReLU-Networks under Convex Relaxations
papers.summary: Studies how expressive ReLU networks are under common convex relaxations, showing more precise relaxations can exactly analyze more univariate functions, yet no single-neuron relaxation precisely analyzes ReLU networks for multivariate convex monotone piecewise-linear functions.

papers.title: GNNCert: Deterministic Certification of Graph Neural Networks against Adversarial Perturbations
papers.summary: GNNCert deterministically certifies graph classifiers against bounded perturbations to both graph structure and node features, guaranteeing the same label when perturbed edges and feature-perturbed nodes are limited; on 8 benchmark datasets it outperforms three prior methods.

papers.title: Incremental Randomized Smoothing Certification
papers.summary: IRS incrementally certifies modified models, such as quantized or pruned versions, under randomized smoothing by reusing the original smoothed model's guarantees with very few samples, achieving up to 3x speedup over recertifying from scratch.

papers.title: Interpreting Robustness Proofs of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Generates human-understandable interpretations of DNN robustness proofs, revealing that proofs for standard networks rely on spurious features, provably robust training filters out even meaningful features, and combined adversarial and provable training best balances the two.

papers.title: LipSim: A Provably Robust Perceptual Similarity Metric
papers.summary: LipSim is a perceptual similarity metric built on 1-Lipschitz networks that certifies its output against all l2-bounded perturbations, after showing ViT ensemble-based metrics are vulnerable to attacks; evaluated on natural and certified scores and image retrieval.

papers.title: Mitigating the Curse of Dimensionality for Certified Robustness via Dual Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Dual Randomized Smoothing down-samples an image into two sub-images and smooths each in lower dimension, proving a tight l2 certified radius for the original input that shrinks more slowly with dimension; improves accuracy and certified robustness on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet.

papers.title: Novel Quadratic Constraints for Extending LipSDP beyond Slope-Restricted Activations
papers.summary: Extends LipSDP to GroupSort, MaxMin and Householder activations with new quadratic constraints, giving a unified SDP for l2 and l-infinity Lipschitz bounds of residual, non-residual and implicit networks that is less conservative than existing approaches.

papers.title: On the Scalability and Memory Efficiency of Semidefinite Programs for Lipschitz Constant Estimation of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Recasts SDP-based Lipschitz constant estimation as an eigenvalue optimization solvable by first-order methods in autodiff frameworks, via redundant quadratic constraints and Lagrangian and Shor relaxations, using far less memory and scaling to large ImageNet networks.

papers.title: Provably Robust Conformal Prediction with Improved Efficiency
papers.summary: Fixes the flawed guarantee of randomized smoothed conformal prediction with RSCP+, certifying coverage of conformal prediction sets under adversarial noise, and adds Post-Training Transformation and Robust Conformal Training to shrink sets, improving efficiency up to 16.9x on ImageNet.

papers.title: The Lipschitz-Variance-Margin Tradeoff for Enhanced Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Improves randomized smoothing certificates by analysing how Monte-Carlo variance interacts with the base classifier's Lipschitz constant and margin, using a new logit-to-probability mapping, Bernstein's inequality and tighter Lipschitz bounds; raises certified accuracy and works zero-shot on pre-trained models.

papers.title: Understanding Certified Training with Interval Bound Propagation
papers.summary: Studies why interval bound propagation (IBP) certified training works, using a new bound-tightness metric; derives conditions for exact IBP bounds that explain the robustness-accuracy trade-off, finds wider ReLU networks perform better, and shows tightness is neither necessary nor sufficient for certifiable robustness.

papers.title: CrossCert: A Cross-Checking Detection Approach to Patch Robustness Certification for Deep Learning Models
papers.summary: CrossCert cross-checks two certified recovery defenders against adversarial patches to give unwavering certification, guaranteeing a benign label without warnings under patching, with detection certification comparable to PatchCensor and slightly below ViP.

papers.title: Harnessing Neuron Stability to Improve DNN Verification
papers.summary: VeriStable extends DPLL-based DNN verification by detecting neurons that become stable during search, cutting combinatorial cost, and adds multi-threading and restarts from SAT solvers; on MNIST and CIFAR FNNs, CNNs and ResNets it outperforms α-β-CROWN and MN-BaB.

months.label: December 2023
months.intro: AAAI 2024 and OOPSLA 2024 decisions: formal explanations, with aggregated and inflated abductive explanations, alongside provable repair for global robustness (REGLO), domain-constraint satisfaction (DeepSaDe) and reward-martingale verification of DRL control systems. VHAGaR computes minimal globally robust bounds via mixed-integer programming.

papers.title: Axiomatic Aggregations of Abductive Explanations
papers.summary: Aggregates the many valid abductive explanations of a prediction into feature importance scores, using two power indices from cooperative game theory and a causal strength measure, each characterized axiomatically; the resulting scores resist attacks that fool SHAP and LIME.

papers.title: DRF: Improving Certified Robustness via Distributional Robustness Framework
papers.summary: DRF links adversarial-training-based randomized smoothing methods to distributional robustness, showing they are special cases of its framework; this gives control over the trade-off between clean accuracy and certified robustness of smoothed classifiers and substantially improves certified robustness.

papers.title: DeepSaDe: Learning Neural Networks That Guarantee Domain Constraint Satisfaction
papers.summary: DeepSaDe trains neural networks that provably satisfy domain constraints on all predictions, extending constraint-satisfaction-based learning of linear models with constraint propagation across layers and weight updates that mix gradient descent and CSP solving; it enforces varied constraints across several tasks.

papers.title: Delivering Inflated Explanations
papers.summary: Defines inflated abductive explanations, which give each selected feature a set of values under which the decision stays unchanged, making formal explanations more informative; they cost little more than abductive explanations to compute, and duality results extend to them.

papers.title: REGLO: Provable Neural Network Repair for Global Robustness Properties
papers.summary: REGLO repairs pretrained ReLU networks to satisfy global robustness and individual fairness; it proves counterexamples must have large gradients, uses this to find violating linear regions, and solves a robust convex optimization problem for a minimal weight change that provably repairs them.

papers.title: Robustness Verification of Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Control Systems Using Reward Martingales
papers.summary: Verifies robustness of deep reinforcement learning control systems under state perturbations with reward martingales, giving certified bounds on expected cumulative reward and on its tails; the martingales are trained as neural networks, and the bounds tightly enclose simulation outcomes.

papers.title: Verification of Neural Networks' Global Robustness
papers.summary: VHAGaR is an anytime verifier that computes the minimal globally robust bound of a classifier by mixed-integer programming, pruned with perturbation and network dependencies and generalized adversarial attacks; within three hours its bound gap averages 1.9 versus 154.7 for a prior verifier, 130.6x faster.

months.label: October 2023
months.intro: ICSE 2024 and POPL 2024 decisions: WraLU over-approximates the ReLU convex hull for verification within PRIMA, and VeRe uses linear-relaxation-based verification to localize faulty neurons and repair deep neural networks.

papers.title: ReLU Hull Approximation
papers.summary: WraLU over-approximates the convex hull of ReLU for neural network verification by wrapping it in a polytope whose upper faces are built from the edges and vertices of the lower faces; integrated into PRIMA, it cuts LP constraints by up to half without losing precision.

papers.title: VeRe: Verification Guided Synthesis for Repairing Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: VeRe repairs deep neural networks by using linear-relaxation-based verification to localize faulty neurons symbolically and then optimizing their parameters; it cuts backdoor attack success from 98.47% to 0.38% on average and repairs all 36 safety-property tasks.

months.label: September 2023
months.intro: NeurIPS 2023, CCS 2023, NDSS 2024 and USENIX Security 2024 decisions: certified training and randomized smoothing lead, from deterministic certification on ImageNet with LiResNet to hierarchical and diffusion-based smoothing. Neural control appears through barrier functions, Lyapunov control and compositional policy learning, while INVPROP bounds preimages, VeriX targets verified explainability, and TextGuard and CBD address backdoors.

papers.title: Machine Learning needs Better Randomness Standards: Randomised Smoothing and PRNG-based attacks
papers.summary: Shows that backdooring the random number generator used by randomised smoothing can make certification over- or underestimate robustness by up to 81 times, with tiny changes that NIST randomness tests miss, and argues for updated NIST guidelines for machine learning.

papers.title: Unraveling the Connections between Privacy and Certified Robustness in Federated Learning Against Poisoning Attacks
papers.summary: Studies how differential privacy in federated learning yields certified robustness against poisoning, giving certified prediction and certified attack inefficacy at user and instance levels; stronger privacy improves certified attack inefficacy but not necessarily certified prediction.

papers.title: TextGuard: Provable Defense against Backdoor Attacks on Text Classification
papers.summary: TextGuard is a provable defense against backdoor attacks on text classification: it splits training sentences into sub-sentences to form sub-training sets, trains an ensemble, and guarantees unchanged predictions when the trigger length is below a threshold, beating prior certified defenses.

papers.title: (Provable) Adversarial Robustness for Group Equivariant Tasks: Graphs, Point Clouds, Molecules, and More
papers.summary: Defines adversarial robustness that accounts for task equivariances such as rotation or permutation, and shows it is provable with equivariant models plus standard certification; introduces equivariance-preserving randomized smoothing and the first graph edit distance certificates for node classification.

papers.title: Asymmetric Certified Robustness via Feature-Convex Neural Networks
papers.summary: Feature-convex neural networks, composing an input-convex network with a Lipschitz feature map, give deterministic closed-form certified radii for any ℓp norm on a sensitive class in asymmetric binary classification, reaching state-of-the-art certified ℓ1 radii on malware and image datasets efficiently.

papers.title: Boosting Verification of Deep Reinforcement Learning via Piece-Wise Linear Decision Neural Networks
CBD: A Certified Backdoor Detector Based on Local Dominant Probability
papers.summary: CBD is a certified backdoor detector based on conformal prediction with a local dominant probability statistic, giving detection conditions and a false positive rate bound; for ℓ2-bounded random triggers it reaches certified true positive rates up to 98% on GTSRB and CIFAR-10.

papers.title: Certifiably Robust Graph Contrastive Learning
papers.summary: Certifies robustness of graph contrastive learning against structure and attribute attacks with RES (Randomized Edgedrop Smoothing), which works for any GCL model and preserves the certificate in downstream tasks; also proposes a training method for robust GCL.

papers.title: Certification of Distributional Individual Fairness
papers.summary: Certifies distributional individual fairness of neural networks, guaranteeing fair predictions for all distributions in a γ-Wasserstein ball around the data, via a convex approximation of individual fairness constraints and quasi-convex optimization; scales to networks orders of magnitude larger than prior work.

papers.title: Certified Robustness via Dynamic Margin Maximization and Improved Lipschitz Regularization
papers.summary: Trains certifiably robust classifiers by enlarging the logit margin while regularizing the Lipschitz constant along vulnerable directions, using a scalable method for differentiable guaranteed Lipschitz upper bounds; reports competitive improvements on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and Tiny-ImageNet.

papers.title: Compositional Policy Learning in Stochastic Control Systems with Formal Guarantees
papers.summary: Learns compositions of neural network policies for stochastic control with a formal certificate that a SpectRL specification holds with a target probability, using reach-avoid supermartingales per sub-task and a tighter reach-avoid probability bound; evaluated on Stochastic Nine Rooms.

papers.title: Connecting Certified and Adversarial Training
Exact Verification of ReLU Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Exactly verifies safety of ReLU neural control barrier functions using a generalized Nagumo theorem for nonsmooth boundaries: the barrier is split into linear segments, each checked by a nonlinear program, with pruning by IBP and linear relaxation; compared against SMT-based methods.

papers.title: Exploiting Connections between Lipschitz Structures for Certifiably Robust Deep Equilibrium Models
Hierarchical Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Hierarchical randomized smoothing certifies models against adversaries that perturb only a subset of entities, such as pixels or nodes, by adding noise to a randomly chosen subset of entities; it gives certificates for discrete and continuous domains with better robustness-accuracy trade-offs.

papers.title: Multi-scale Diffusion Denoised Smoothing
papers.summary: Improves denoised smoothing with diffusion models by selectively smoothing across multiple noise scales with one diffusion model, plus fine-tuning it to denoise consistently when the image is recoverable; this gives strong certified robustness at high noise while keeping accuracy near non-smoothed classifiers.

papers.title: Neural Lyapunov Control for Discrete-Time Systems
papers.summary: Learns provably stable neural Lyapunov controllers for discrete-time nonlinear systems, verifying Lyapunov conditions with mixed-integer linear programming, computing verified sublevel sets and finding counterexamples by gradient search; it beats baselines by an order of magnitude on path tracking.

papers.title: Provably Bounding Neural Network Preimages
papers.summary: INVPROP over-approximates neural network preimages, the inputs that lead to a linearly constrained output set, on GPU without an LP solver and with branch-and-bound; in some settings it is over 2500x tighter and 2.5x faster than prior work, and ships in α,β-CROWN.

papers.title: RS-Del: Edit Distance Robustness Certificates for Sequence Classifiers via Randomized Deletion
papers.summary: RS-Del certifies sequence classifiers against edit-distance-bounded adversaries via randomized deletion smoothing, with a certification proof built on longest common subsequences; on the MalConv malware detector it reaches 91% certified accuracy at an edit distance radius of 128 bytes.

papers.title: Stability Guarantees for Feature Attributions with Multiplicative Smoothing
papers.summary: Multiplicative Smoothing (MuS) makes a classifier Lipschitz with respect to feature masking, which provably yields relaxed stability guarantees for feature attributions; it works with any classifier and attribution method, including LIME and SHAP, on vision and language models.

papers.title: Temporal Robustness against Data poisoning
papers.summary: Proposes a temporal threat model for data poisoning based on data timestamps, with earliness and duration metrics, defines temporal robustness, provides a benchmark simulating continual data collection, and gives a temporal aggregation baseline with provable temporal robustness even against unbounded poisoned samples.

papers.title: UniT: A Unified Look at Certified Robust Training against Text Adversarial Perturbation
Unlocking Deterministic Robustness Certification on ImageNet
papers.summary: Scales deterministic Lipschitz-based robustness certification to ImageNet with the LiResNet architecture, whose residual block admits tight Lipschitz bounds, and the EMMA loss that penalizes worst-case adversaries from all classes; also gives the best ℓ2 certified accuracy on CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny-ImageNet.

papers.title: VeriX: Towards Verified Explainability of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: VeriX computes optimal robust explanations and counterfactuals along decision boundaries of machine learning models, building them iteratively with constraint solving and a feature-level sensitivity ranking heuristic; evaluated on image recognition benchmarks and autonomous aircraft taxiing.

months.label: July 2023
months.intro: ASE 2023, ICCV 2023 and S&P 2024 decisions: faster verification through network reduction and HOBAT's batch verification of homogeneous networks, Text-CRS certification against word-level textual attacks, TrajPAC for pedestrian trajectory prediction, and disaggregated measures of certified robustness.

papers.title: It's Simplex! Disaggregating Measures to Improve Certified Robustness
papers.summary: Argues that aggregate metrics hide per-sample behaviour of certified robustness and proposes dataset-independent and dataset-dependent analyses based on the output space of certified models; these lead to new certification approaches that certify 9% more samples at noise scale σ = 1.

papers.title: Text-CRS: A Generalized Certified Robustness Framework against Textual Adversarial Attacks
papers.summary: Text-CRS certifies text classifiers against synonym substitution, word reordering, insertion and deletion via randomized smoothing, modelling each word-level operation as permutation plus embedding transformation with tailored noise distributions; it also gives the first certified accuracy benchmark for these four operations.

papers.title: TrajPAC: Towards Robustness Verification of Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction Models
papers.summary: TrajPAC verifies robustness of pedestrian trajectory prediction models with a probably approximately correct (PAC) framework, after formally defining label and pure robustness; it finds counterexamples and evaluates Trajectron++, MemoNet, AgentFormer and MID on ETH/UCY and Stanford Drone scenes.

papers.title: Expediting Neural Network Verification via Network Reduction
papers.summary: Speeds up neural network verification by removing stable ReLU neurons and converting networks into sequential ReLU and affine layers before verification; applied with α,β-crown, VeriNet and PRIMA, it shrinks networks, accelerates verification and lets tools handle more architectures.

papers.title: HOBAT: Batch Verification for Homogeneous Structural Neural Networks
papers.summary: HOBAT verifies batches of structurally homogeneous neural networks, such as candidates produced by continual learning, by abstracting same-position neurons across the batch into one neuron and refining iteratively; combined with bound propagation, it significantly improves on the vanilla approach.

months.label: June 2023
months.intro: OOPSLA 2023 decisions: Calzone, a sound and complete few-pixel (L0) robustness verifier, and perception contracts that bound perception errors to keep controllers using neural perception safe.

papers.title: Deep Learning Robustness Verification for Few-Pixel Attacks
papers.summary: Calzone is a sound and complete L0 (few-pixel) robustness verifier that predicts the largest provable pixel-set size, covers the image with covering designs and checks each set with an L∞ verifier; it typically finishes in minutes, while a MILP baseline fails at t=3.

papers.title: Perception Contracts for Safety of ML-Enabled Systems
papers.summary: Introduces perception contracts, bounds on perception errors that preserve safety invariants of controllers using neural perception, with symbolic learning algorithms that synthesize them from images; evaluated on lane tracking for an electric vehicle and a crop-row-following agricultural robot.

months.label: May 2023
months.intro: ISSTA 2023 and USENIX Security 2023 decisions: DualApp tightens over-approximation via under-approximation, GCERT certifies against semantic image mutations, and provable defenses target adversarial policies in two-player games (PATROL) and data poisoning of recommender systems (PORE).

papers.title: A Tale of Two Approximations: Tightening Over-Approximation for DNN Robustness Verification via Under-Approximation
papers.summary: DualApp tightens linear over-approximations of activation functions for DNN robustness verification by using an under-approximated actual domain, computed via Monte Carlo simulation or gradient descent; it improves verified robustness ratio by 100%-1000% and certified lower bounds by 10.64% on average.

papers.title: PATROL: Provable Defense against Adversarial Policy in Two-player Games
PORE: Provably Robust Recommender Systems against Data Poisoning Attacks
papers.summary: PORE makes any recommender system provably robust to untargeted data poisoning: it guarantees that at least r of the top-N items recommended without attack remain recommended, where r depends on the number of fake users and is computed efficiently per user.

papers.title: Precise and Generalized Robustness Certification for Neural Networks
papers.summary: GCERT certifies neural network robustness against semantic image mutations, such as weather filters, style transfer and perceptual changes, by expressing them as directions in a generative model's latent space; it plugs into complete, incomplete and quantitative certification frameworks.

months.label: April 2023
months.intro: CAV 2023, ICML 2023 and IJCAI 2023 decisions: Lipschitz bounds and certified training are a main theme, alongside formal explanations for monotonic networks and planning policies. CAV adds NNV 2.0, QEBVerif for quantization error bounds and hybrid controller synthesis, while IJCAI defines #DNN-Verification for counting unsafe inputs.

papers.title: Cardinality-Minimal Explanations for Monotonic Neural Networks
papers.summary: Shows that cardinality-minimal abductive and contrastive explanations, intractable in general and still hard for monotonic networks, become computable in polynomial time by greedy algorithms when activations are continuous and almost everywhere differentiable; experiments indicate favourable performance.

papers.title: Formal Explanations of Neural Network Policies for Planning
papers.summary: Formulates formal explanations for sequences of decisions made by neural network planning policies and shows that, under assumptions, a minimal explanation needs a number of single-decision explanation problems linear in sequence length; implemented for ASNet policies on classical planning domains.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Logic Shields
papers.summary: Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) shields deep RL agents by encoding safety constraints as differentiable functions through probabilistic logic programming, works with any policy gradient algorithm while keeping convergence guarantees, and learns safer, higher-reward policies than other shielding methods.

papers.title: The #DNN-Verification Problem: Counting Unsafe Inputs for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Defines #DNN-Verification, counting the inputs that violate a safety property of a deep neural network; shows #P-completeness, gives an exact counting method and a randomized approximate method with a provable probabilistic bound, evaluated on safety-critical benchmarks.

papers.title: Hybrid Controller Synthesis for Nonlinear Systems Subject to Reach-Avoid Constraints
papers.summary: Synthesizes provably correct hybrid polynomial-DNN controllers for nonlinear systems with reach-avoid requirements, combining RL, low-degree polynomial fitting and knowledge distillation, and solving constrained optimization for barrier certificates and Lyapunov-like functions; evaluated on benchmarks including high-dimensional systems.

papers.title: NNV 2.0: The Neural Network Verification Tool
papers.summary: NNV 2.0 extends the NNV verification tool to neural ODEs, semantic segmentation and recurrent networks, adds cheaper reachability methods and VNNLIB and ONNX support, and verifies safety and robustness across control, segmentation, image classification and time-series benchmarks, compared with a commercial product.

papers.title: QEBVerif: Quantization Error Bound Verification of Neural Networks
papers.summary: QEBVerif verifies quantization error bounds between a DNN and its fully quantized counterpart, using differential reachability analysis layer by layer and falling back to an equivalent MILP encoding when that fails, making the method sound and complete.

papers.title: Verifying Generalization in Deep Learning
papers.summary: Uses DNN verification to judge how well DNN decision rules generalize to new input domains, measuring agreement among independently trained networks on that domain; evaluated on three deep reinforcement learning benchmarks, including Internet congestion control.

papers.title: A Robust Optimisation Perspective on Counterexample-Guided Repair of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Views counterexample-guided neural network repair as robust optimisation, proving termination for restricted models and disproving it in general; empirically shows common verifiers and falsifiers still suit repair, and gives a quadratic-programming repair algorithm for linear regression.

papers.title: BNN-DP: Robustness Certification of Bayesian Neural Networks via Dynamic Programming
Certifying Ensembles: A General Certification Theory with S-Lipschitzness
papers.summary: Introduces S-Lipschitz classifiers, a generalization of Lipschitz continuity, to analyse certified robustness of ensembles, deriving precise conditions under which an ensemble of robust classifiers is more robust, or less robust, than each of its members.

papers.title: Dimension-independent Certified Neural Network Watermarks via Mollifier Smoothing
papers.summary: Certifies neural network watermarks against ℓp-norm removal attacks for all p from 1 to infinity with mollifier smoothing, whose certified radius is independent of parameter dimension; a PDE-based approximation reduces the sampling and numerical integration cost.

papers.title: Direct Parameterization of Lipschitz-Bounded Deep Networks
papers.summary: Gives a direct, complete parameterization of fully-connected and convolutional networks meeting the SDP-based ℓ2 Lipschitz bound, as sandwich layers trainable with standard gradient methods; outperforms prior approaches on empirical and certified robust accuracy in image classification.

papers.title: Efficient Bound of Lipschitz Constant for Convolutional Layers by Gram Iteration
papers.summary: Gram iteration gives a precise, fast, differentiable upper bound on the spectral norm of convolutional layers via circulant matrix theory, converging superlinearly; it beats other methods in precision, cost and scalability and works well for Lipschitz regularization of CNNs.

papers.title: FARE: Provably Fair Representation Learning with Practical Certificates
Improving l1-Certified Robustness via Randomized Smoothing by Leveraging Box Constraints
papers.summary: Improves ℓ1-certified robustness of randomized smoothing by deriving certification formulae that exploit the fact that adversarial images must lie in the image space [0,1]^d, giving significant gains without changing classifiers or smoothing distributions.

papers.title: Robust One-Class Classification with Signed Distance Function using 1-Lipschitz Neural Networks
papers.summary: OCSDF performs one-class classification by learning the signed distance function to a distribution's support with 1-Lipschitz networks, giving ℓ2 robustness bounds and a certified AUROC metric; it is competitive on tabular and image data while much more robust to attacks.

papers.title: Run-off Election: Improved Provable Defense against Data Poisoning Attacks
papers.summary: Run-Off Election aggregates ensemble defenses against data poisoning with a two-round vote using base models' logits, yielding DPA+ROE and FA+ROE; certified accuracy improves by up to 3-4% on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and GTSRB, and 12-27% with boosted DPA.

papers.title: Tight Certification of Adversarially Trained Neural Networks via Nonconvex Low-Rank Semidefinite Relaxations
papers.summary: Certifies adversarially trained networks with a nonconvex low-rank restriction of the SDP relaxation, matching expensive SDP certificates with far fewer variables and reaching global optimality via local optimization in polynomial time; it nearly closes the gap to exact certification.

months.label: March 2023
months.intro: S&P 2023 decisions: certified defenses against patch hiding attacks on object detection (ObjectSeeker) and against backdoor attacks (RAB), plus a systematization of certified robustness for deep neural networks.

papers.title: ObjectSeeker: Certifiably Robust Object Detection against Patch Hiding Attacks via Patch-agnostic Masking
papers.summary: ObjectSeeker certifies object detectors against patch hiding attacks through patch-agnostic masking that removes the patch without knowing its shape, size or location; certified robustness improves by about 10-40% absolute over prior work with roughly 1% clean performance drop.

papers.title: RAB: Provable Robustness Against Backdoor Attacks
papers.summary: RAB certifies robustness against backdoor attacks through a randomized smoothing framework and smoothed training with a proven tight bound, plus an exact smooth-training algorithm for K-NN; gives the first certified backdoor robustness benchmark on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNette.

papers.title: SoK: Certified Robustness for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Systematization of certifiably robust approaches for deep neural networks: a taxonomy of robustness verification and robust training methods, their strengths, limits and connections, open challenges, and an open-source platform benchmarking more than 20 representative approaches.

months.label: February 2023
months.intro: CVPR 2023 and PLDI 2023 decisions: PLDI brings CRAFT's abstract interpretation of fixpoint iterators, APRNN's architecture-preserving repair and IVAN's incremental verification. CVPR covers verified training via abstraction, verification against latent-variable-model specifications and PointCert for point cloud classification.

papers.title: Abstract Interpretation of Fixpoint Iterators with Applications to Neural Networks
papers.summary: CRAFT over-approximates fixpoints of numerical iterators via abstract interpretation without joins, using a new CH-Zonotope domain; on monDEQ neural networks it is two orders of magnitude faster, one order more scalable and 25% higher in certified accuracy than prior work.

papers.title: Architecture-Preserving Provable Repair of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: APRNN provably repairs DNNs over V-polytope specifications by changing only parameters, possibly across multiple layers, in polynomial time, supporting piecewise-linear activations and convolutional, pooling and residual layers; it beats PRDNN and REASSURE on MNIST, ImageNet and ACAS Xu.

papers.title: Incremental Verification of Neural Networks
papers.summary: IVAN makes complete DNN verification incremental, reusing work from verifying the original network when it is updated, via new theory, data structures and algorithms; it achieves geometric mean speedups of 2.4x on MNIST and CIFAR10 and 3.8x on ACAS-XU.

papers.title: Boosting Verified Training for Robust Image Classifications via Abstraction
papers.summary: Certified training that maps perturbed images to intervals before training, smoothing the loss landscape, and enables sound and complete black-box verification; it reduces verified errors by up to 95.64%, gives up to 602.50x speedup and scales to 138-million-parameter models.

papers.title: Efficient Verification of Neural Networks Against LVM-Based Specifications
papers.summary: Verifies neural networks against specifications defined by latent variable models that capture pose, viewpoint and occlusion changes, by attaching an invertible encoding head so latent-space sets can be verified with little reconstruction overhead; scales largely independently of input dimension.

papers.title: PointCert: Point Cloud Classification with Deterministic Certified Robustness Guarantees
papers.summary: PointCert turns any point cloud classifier into one with deterministic certified robustness, keeping the label when fewer than a threshold number of points are added, deleted or modified; it outperforms probabilistic certified defenses on ModelNet and ScanObjectNN.

months.label: January 2023
months.intro: ICLR 2023, ICRA 2023 and USENIX Security 2023 decisions: randomized smoothing leads, with diffusion-based denoised smoothing (DensePure, DiffSmooth), DMAE and localized smoothing. Certified training covers small boxes, SDP-based Lipschitz Layers and geometric transformations, and ICRA adds reachability analysis of neural network dynamical systems, including ReachLipBnB.

papers.title: (Certified!!) Adversarial Robustness for Free!
papers.summary: Achieves certified ℓ2 robustness with only off-the-shelf models through denoised smoothing that pairs a pretrained diffusion model with a standard classifier, certifying 71% ImageNet accuracy at radius 0.5, 14 points above the prior best, without fine-tuning.

papers.title: A Unified Algebraic Perspective on Lipschitz Neural Networks
papers.summary: Unifies many 1-Lipschitz layer designs as analytical solutions of a common SDP condition and, with the Gershgorin circle theorem, derives new parameterizations called SDP-based Lipschitz Layers (SLL), which outperform previous approaches in certified robust accuracy on image classification.

papers.title: Certifiably Robust Policy Learning against Adversarial Multi-Agent Communication
Certified Defences Against Adversarial Patch Attacks on Semantic Segmentation
papers.summary: Demasked Smoothing certifies semantic segmentation models against adversarial patches without retraining or architecture changes, supporting certified detection and recovery; on ADE20K it certifies 64% of pixel predictions for a 1% patch in detection and 48% for a 0.5% patch in recovery.

papers.title: Certified Training: Small Boxes are All You Need
Denoising Masked Autoencoders Help Robust Classification
papers.summary: Denoising Masked AutoEncoders (DMAE) pre-train a Transformer encoder to reconstruct images corrupted by Gaussian noise and masking, then use it as the base classifier for Gaussian smoothing; DMAE ViT-Large sets new certified accuracy records on ImageNet and transfers to CIFAR-10.

papers.title: DensePure: Understanding Diffusion Models for Adversarial Robustness
Efficient Certified Training and Robustness Verification of Neural ODEs
Fundamental Limits in Formal Verification of Message-Passing Neural Networks
papers.summary: Proves that output reachability of graph-classifier message-passing neural networks over unbounded graphs cannot be formally verified, while output reachability and adversarial robustness of node-classifier MPNNs become verifiable when the degree of input graphs is bounded in advance.

papers.title: Localized Randomized Smoothing for Collective Robustness Certification
papers.summary: Localized randomized smoothing gives collective robustness certificates for multi-output models such as segmentation and node classification, scaling noise per input region by its importance to each output; it Pareto-dominates existing certificates in accuracy and certificate strength.

papers.title: On the Perils of Cascading Robust Classifiers
papers.summary: Shows that the robustness certifier of cascading ensembles of certifiably robust networks is unsound and presents the CasA attack, which finds adversarial inputs for up to 88% of samples claimed certifiably robust and drops accuracy to as low as 11%.

papers.title: Provable Defense Against Geometric Transformations
papers.summary: Provides the first deterministic certified training against geometric transformations such as scaling and rotation, using a GPU-optimized verifier 60x to 42,600x faster than existing ones; trained networks reach top certified geometric robustness and clean accuracy, including for autonomous driving.

papers.title: Provable Robustness against Wasserstein Distribution Shifts via Input Randomization
Robust Explanation Constraints for Neural Networks
papers.summary: Certifies the robustness of gradient-based explanations against bounded input or parameter manipulation by propagating symbolic intervals through forward and backward passes; the differentiable bounds enable training, yielding explanation-robustness certificates on all six datasets tested.

papers.title: Sound Randomized Smoothing in Floating-Point Arithmetic
Towards Robustness Certification Against Universal Perturbations
papers.summary: Certifies neural network robustness against universal perturbations shared across all samples, combining linear relaxation-based perturbation analysis with MILP, plus population-level error bounds from a sampled batch; supports comparing defenses and detecting backdoor target classes.

papers.title: Wasserstein Auto-encoded MDPs: Formal Verification of Efficiently Distilled RL Policies with Many-sided Guarantees
papers.summary: WAE-MDP distils RL policies into discrete latent models by minimising a penalised optimal-transport distance, giving bisimulation guarantees so formal verification transfers to the distilled policy; distillation runs up to 10 times faster with better latent model quality.

papers.title: DiffSmooth: Certifiably Robust Learning via Diffusion Models and Local Smoothing
papers.summary: DiffSmooth certifies classifiers by purifying inputs with diffusion models and then applying local smoothing, backed by analysis bounding recovered instances near the original; it raises certified ImageNet accuracy at ℓ2 radius 1.5 from 36.0% to 53.0%.

papers.title: One-Shot Reachability Analysis of Neural Network Dynamical Systems
papers.summary: Reachability analysis of neural network dynamical systems that verifies the unrolled system in one shot rather than recursively propagating bounds, proven to reduce compounding over-approximation error; the performance gap is characterised and demonstrated on a cart-pole system.

papers.title: ReachLipBnB: A branch-and-bound method for reachability analysis of neural autonomous systems using Lipschitz bounds
papers.summary: ReachLipBnB computes reachable sets of neural networks and neural-network-controlled systems using directional Lipschitz bounds from a convex program inside branch-and-bound, with PCA on sampled trajectories to choose polyhedral directions; evaluated in open- and closed-loop settings.

months.label: December 2022
months.intro: ICSE 2023 decisions: fairness verification with Fairify, which checks individual fairness of neural networks with SMT, partitioning the input domain and pruning neurons to return certificates or counterexamples.

papers.title: Fairify: Fairness Verification of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Fairify verifies individual fairness of neural networks with SMT, partitioning the input domain and pruning neurons per partition via interval arithmetic and activation heuristics to return certificates or counterexamples; evaluated on 25 real-world networks from four sources.

months.label: November 2022
months.intro: AAAI 2023 decisions: formal explanations stand out, with background knowledge for shorter explanations and a feature relevancy algorithm. Other work covers CertiFair for global fairness of ReLU classifiers, confidence-aware training of smoothed classifiers, pointwise certification against poisoning, and control policies with reach-avoid guarantees for stochastic systems.

papers.title: CertiFair: A Framework for Certified Global Fairness of Neural Networks
papers.summary: CertiFair is a sound and complete verifier for global individual fairness of ReLU classifiers under distance-based similarity, returning counterexamples when violated, plus a fairness loss for provably fair training; global individual fairness improves by 96% without significant accuracy loss.

papers.title: Confidence-Aware Training of Smoothed Classifiers for Certified Robustness
papers.summary: Training method for randomized-smoothing classifiers that uses accuracy under Gaussian noise as a per-sample proxy for robustness, filtering out samples unlikely to benefit from the adversarial objective; consistently improves certified l2 robustness over earlier training methods.

papers.title: Eliminating the Impossible, Whatever Remains Must Be True: On Extracting and Applying Background Knowledge in the Context of Formal Explanations
papers.summary: Uses background knowledge extracted from data with rule induction to make formal explanations of ML predictions shorter for why questions and more accurate for why-not questions, dropping the assumption that features are independent and uniformly distributed.

papers.title: Enhancing the Antidote: Improved Pointwise Certifications against Poisoning Attacks
papers.summary: Pointwise certification against poisoning attacks that modify a bounded number of training samples, built on differential privacy and the Sampled Gaussian Mechanism; the certified robustness guarantees are more than twice as large as those of earlier certifications.

papers.title: Learning Control Policies for Stochastic Systems with Reach-Avoid Guarantees
papers.summary: Learns controllers for discrete-time nonlinear stochastic systems with infinite-horizon probabilistic reach-avoid guarantees, using neural reach-avoid supermartingales as certificates; supports learning policies from scratch, verifying fixed policies or fine-tuning, validated on 3 stochastic RL tasks.

papers.title: Solving Explainability Queries with Quantification: The Case of Feature Relevancy
papers.summary: Algorithm for the feature relevancy problem, deciding whether a feature can appear in some explanation of a prediction, applicable to any classifier meeting minor requirements; on random forests it outperforms QBF solvers by orders of magnitude.

months.label: October 2022
months.intro: NDSS 2023 decisions: BARS certifies local robustness of deep-learning traffic analysis systems with boundary-adaptive randomized smoothing.

papers.title: BARS: Local Robustness Certification for Deep Learning based Traffic Analysis Systems
papers.summary: BARS certifies local robustness of deep-learning traffic analysis systems via boundary-adaptive randomized smoothing, optimising noise shape and scale with a Distribution Transformer and gradient-based search; gives tighter guarantees than baselines on three practical traffic analysis systems.

months.label: September 2022
months.intro: NeurIPS 2022 decisions: randomized smoothing leads, extended to graph neural networks, multi-label and few-shot models and model invariances. Lipschitz networks and certified training follow with LOT and CRT, while complete verification advances through GCP-CROWN cutting planes and VPN for polynomial networks. Control work adds neural abstractions, neural Lyapunov control and stochastic barrier functions, alongside certified defenses against data poisoning such as BagFlip.

papers.title: A Quantitative Geometric Approach to Neural-Network Smoothness
papers.summary: Quantitative geometric framework for Lipschitz constant estimation of neural networks, yielding hardness and approximability results and SDP-based algorithms in the tool GeoLIP, which is more scalable and precise than existing tools for l-infinity perturbations.

papers.title: Accelerating Certified Robustness Training via Knowledge Transfer
papers.summary: Certified Robustness Transfer (CRT) cuts the cost of certified training by transferring robustness from a robust teacher to a student through a new loss; on CIFAR-10 it speeds training by 8x on average with comparable robustness, and scales to ImageNet.

papers.title: BagFlip: A Certified Defense Against Data Poisoning
papers.summary: BagFlip is a model-agnostic certified defense against data poisoning that handles both trigger-less and backdoor attacks; on image classification and malware detection it matches or beats prior approaches for trigger-less attacks and beats them for backdoor attacks.

papers.title: Certifying Robust Graph Classification under Orthogonal Gromov-Wasserstein Threats
Certifying Some Distributional Fairness with Subpopulation Decomposition
papers.summary: Certifies distributional fairness of ML models by bounding performance loss on fairness-constrained distributions near the training distribution, decomposing data into analytical subpopulations with convex subproblems; tight under sensitive shifting and non-trivial under general shifting on six datasets.

papers.title: CoPur: Certifiably Robust Collaborative Inference via Feature Purification
Double Bubble, Toil and Trouble: Enhancing Certified Robustness through Transitivity
papers.summary: Improves randomized-smoothing l2 certificates by exploiting transitivity of certifications and input-space geometry, called Geometrically-Informed Certified Robustness; certifications improve for more than 80% of Tiny-Imagenet instances, by 5% on average.

papers.title: Efficiently Computing Local Lipschitz Constants of Neural Networks via Bound Propagation
papers.summary: Computes l-infinity local Lipschitz constants of neural networks by linear bound propagation over a backward graph of the Clarke Jacobian, with tight relaxations and branch-and-bound; yields tighter bounds than relaxed methods and scales to larger models, with monotonicity analysis applications.

papers.title: General Cutting Planes for Bound-Propagation-Based Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: GCP-CROWN extends bound propagation in branch-and-bound neural network verification to arbitrary cutting planes, using cuts from MIP solvers on CPU alongside GPU bounding; first to fully solve oval20 and verifies twice as many oval21 instances as the best VNN-COMP 2021 tool.

papers.title: Improved techniques for deterministic l2 robustness
papers.summary: Improves deterministic l2 certified robustness of 1-Lipschitz CNNs by replacing the last linear layer with a 1-hidden-layer MLP, faster Skew Orthogonal Convolution training and new pooling layers; provable robust accuracy rises 3.82% on CIFAR-10 and 4.75% on CIFAR-100.

papers.title: Improving Certified Robustness via Statistical Learning with Logical Reasoning
papers.summary: Improves certified robustness by combining statistical ML models with logical rules through Markov logic networks; proves certifying MLN robustness is #P-hard, derives the first certified bound for MLN, and outperforms prior methods on five image and text datasets.

papers.title: Invariance-Aware Randomized Smoothing Certificates
papers.summary: Gray-box randomized smoothing certificates that exploit model invariances such as permutation and Euclidean isometries, using group orbits plus provably tight certificates; tight certificates give much stronger guarantees, while the orbit-based method is a good practical approximation.

papers.title: LOT: Layer-wise Orthogonal Training on Improving l2 Certified Robustness
papers.summary: LOT trains 1-Lipschitz convolution layers by parametrising orthogonal matrices and computing inverse square roots in the Fourier domain, with semi-supervised learning; raises deterministic l2 certified robustness, e.g. from 59.04% to 63.50% on CIFAR-10 at radius 36/255.

papers.title: Lethal Dose Conjecture on Data Poisoning
papers.summary: Lethal Dose Conjecture: if n clean samples suffice for accurate prediction, only Theta(N/n) poisoned samples out of N can be tolerated; implies DPA and FA defenses are asymptotically optimal, and data augmentation doubles or triples DPA certified robustness on CIFAR-10 and GTSRB.

papers.title: MultiGuard: Provably Robust Multi-label Classification against Adversarial Examples
papers.summary: MultiGuard certifies multi-label classifiers against l2-bounded adversarial perturbations by randomized smoothing with isotropic Gaussian noise, proving a number of ground-truth labels provably stay in the predicted set; evaluated on VOC 2007, MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE.

papers.title: Neural Abstractions
papers.summary: Safety verification of nonlinear dynamical models using neural networks as formal abstractions: CEGIS synthesises ReLU neural ODEs with certified error bounds, verified as affine hybrid automata in SpaceEx; performs comparably to Flow* and handles non-Lipschitz models.

papers.title: Neural Lyapunov Control of Unknown Nonlinear Systems with Stability Guarantees
papers.summary: Learns a neural controller for unknown nonlinear systems together with a neural Lyapunov function certifying a region of attraction, using one network to learn dynamics, another for the controller and Lyapunov function, and an SMT solver to verify Lyapunov conditions.

papers.title: Pay attention to your loss : understanding misconceptions about Lipschitz neural networks
Provable Defense against Backdoor Policies in Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Provable defense against backdoor policies in reinforcement learning that sanitises the policy by projecting observed states onto a safe subspace estimated from few clean interactions, achieving epsilon-approximate optimality under triggers with bounded sample needs; tested on two Atari games.

papers.title: Provably Adversarially Robust Detection of Out-of-Distribution Data (Almost) for Free
Randomized Message-Interception Smoothing: Gray-box Certificates for Graph Neural Networks
papers.summary: Gray-box randomized smoothing certificates for graph neural networks that randomly intercept messages and analyse whether adversarial nodes reach targets, certifying robustness against adversaries controlling entire nodes; graph sparsification further improves certifiable robustness.

papers.title: Rethinking Lipschitz Neural Networks and Certified Robustness: A Boolean Function Perspective
papers.summary: Studies certified l-infinity robustness of Lipschitz networks through Boolean function representation, proving impossibility results for standard Lipschitz networks and explaining how order statistics bypass them; a unified Lipschitz network gives better certified robustness across datasets and radii.

papers.title: Safety Guarantees for Neural Network Dynamic Systems via Stochastic Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Safety guarantees for neural network dynamic models via stochastic barrier functions synthesised by sum-of-squares optimisation over piecewise-linear NN bounds, giving a lower bound on safety probability, plus linear-programming control synthesis; scales to multi-layer models with hundreds of neurons per layer.

papers.title: Shield Decentralization for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Smoothed Embeddings for Certified Few-Shot Learning
papers.summary: Extends randomized smoothing to few-shot learning models that map inputs to normalised embeddings, analysing their Lipschitz continuity to derive robustness certificates against l2-bounded perturbations; the theory is confirmed by experiments on several datasets.

papers.title: Sound and Complete Verification of Polynomial Networks
papers.summary: VPN is a sound and complete verifier for polynomial networks that pairs a new bounding method with branch and bound, producing much tighter bounds than IBP and DeepT-Fast; validated on MNIST, CIFAR10 and STL10.

papers.title: Toward Robust Spiking Neural Network Against Adversarial Perturbation
papers.summary: Certified robust training for spiking neural networks with S-IBP and S-CROWN, bound propagation methods handling spiking neuron nonlinearities, with bounds for digital and spike inputs; reduces attack error by up to 37.7% at 3.7% accuracy loss.

papers.title: Zonotope Domains for Lagrangian Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Neural network verification that uses zonotopes within a Lagrangian decomposition, splitting a deep network into many 2-layer subproblems solved by efficient relaxations and dual ascent; bounds beat linear programming and Lagrangian-based methods in both time and tightness.

months.label: July 2022
months.intro: ASE 2022 and ECCV 2022 decisions: ECCV brought randomized smoothing work, including UniCR, ViP for patch attacks with vision transformers and LASSI for certified individual fairness, plus almost-orthogonal Lipschitz layers. ASE added QVIP, an ILP-based verifier for quantized neural networks, and provably tightest linear approximations for sigmoid-like networks.

papers.title: A Spectral View of Randomized Smoothing Under Common Corruptions: Benchmarking and Improving Certified Robustness
Almost-Orthogonal Layers for Efficient General-Purpose Lipschitz Networks
Latent Space Smoothing for Individually Fair Representations
papers.summary: LASSI learns representations that certify individual fairness for high-dimensional data, capturing similar individuals in a generative latent space, training with adversarial learning and applying randomized smoothing; certified individual fairness on real image data rises by up to 90%.

papers.title: UniCR: Universally Approximated Certified Robustness via Randomized Smoothing
ViP: Unified Certified Detection and Recovery for Patch Attack with Vision Transformers
Provably Tightest Linear Approximation for Robustness Verification of Sigmoid-like Neural Networks
papers.summary: Defines network-wise tightness for linear approximations of sigmoid-like activations in robustness verification and gives two efficient, provably tightest approximations; certified lower robustness bounds improve by up to 251.28%, with more precise results on convolutional networks.

papers.title: QVIP: An ILP-based Formal Verification Approach for Quantized Neural Networks
papers.summary: QVIP verifies quantized neural networks with a sound and complete encoding into integer linear constraints solved off the shelf, applied to local robustness and maximum robustness radius; it is two orders of magnitude faster than prior methods and solves more tasks.

months.label: June 2022
months.intro: IROS 2022 and OOPSLA 2022 decisions: proof transfer is a common thread, with FANC reusing robustness proofs for quantized or pruned networks and vegas verifying GNN-based job schedulers. On the control side, almost-barrier functions quantify safety of learned self-driving controllers.

papers.title: Quantifying Safety of Learning-based Self-Driving Control Using Almost-Barrier Functions
papers.summary: Quantifies safety of neural path-tracking controllers for self-driving by learning almost-barrier functions, certified with neural network robustness analysis in an adversarial learning-certification loop; also builds online safety monitors, tested from kinematic models up to the TORCS simulator.

papers.title: Proof transfer for fast certification of multiple approximate neural networks
papers.summary: FANC transfers robustness proofs from a neural network to its quantized or pruned approximate versions by building templates, symbolic shapes at intermediate layers that capture the proof; verification with DeepZ speeds up by up to 4.1x.

papers.title: Scalable verification of GNN-based job schedulers
papers.summary: vegas verifies single-step and multi-step properties such as strategy-proofness, sharing incentive and stability of GNN-based job schedulers by combining abstraction, refinement, solvers and proof transfer; it gives significant speed-ups over earlier methods.

months.label: May 2022
months.intro: ICML 2022 decisions: randomized smoothing dominates, from Double Sampling Randomized Smoothing and bounded-support smoothing to GSmooth and TPC for semantic transformations, plus watermarks, NLP and image retrieval. Lipschitz and certified training work includes the Convex Potential Layer, CerDEQ and linearity grafting, with FairSmooth for group fairness and Finite Aggregation against data poisoning.

papers.title: A Dynamical System Perspective for Lipschitz Neural Networks
papers.summary: Builds 1-Lipschitz neural networks by viewing residual networks as continuous-time dynamical systems, introducing the Convex Potential Layer from convex-potential ResNet flows; experiments show scalability and benefits as a provable l2 defense against adversarial examples.

papers.title: CerDEQ: Certifiable Deep Equilibrium Model
papers.summary: CerDEQ enables certified training of deep equilibrium models by bounding outputs through bound propagation with the adjoint DEQ, plus weight orthogonalisation; at epsilon 8/255 it reaches 64.72% certified error on CIFAR-10 and 94.45% on Tiny ImageNet.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness Under the Bounded Support Set
