papers.summary: Certifies robustness of neural networks to weight perturbations by computing a bound within which outputs cannot be adversarially changed, and links this to weight quantization, yielding a robustness-aware quantization scheme that improves generalization of quantized networks.

months.label: September 2019
months.intro: NeurIPS 2019 decisions: convex relaxations come under scrutiny, with an exact study revealing an inherent barrier and k-ReLU's multi-neuron relaxations moving beyond it. Randomized smoothing gains adversarial training and tighter certificates, and other directions include DEEPG for geometric robustness, certificates for graph perturbations, GeoCert's exact pointwise robustness, SDP-based Lipschitz bounds and Neural Lyapunov Control.

papers.title: A Convex Relaxation Barrier to Tight Robustness Verification of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Unifies LP-relaxed verifiers under one convex relaxation framework with primal-dual strong duality, then solves the optimal relaxation exactly using over 22 CPU-years, finding it barely narrows the gap to PGD on MNIST and CIFAR networks: an inherent barrier.

papers.title: Abstraction based Output Range Analysis for Neural Networks
papers.summary: Computes output ranges of ReLU feed-forward networks by abstracting them into smaller interval neural networks with interval weights that over-approximate the output range, then solving a mixed integer linear program; experiments show the time-precision trade-off.

papers.title: Beyond the Single Neuron Convex Barrier for Neural Network Certification
papers.summary: k-ReLU computes convex relaxations of multiple ReLUs in a layer jointly rather than one at a time, overcoming the single-neuron triangle relaxation barrier; combined with existing verifiers, it certifies significantly more precisely while staying scalable.

papers.title: Certifiable Robustness to Graph Perturbations
papers.summary: The first method to certify robustness and non-robustness of graph neural networks and label/feature propagation to graph structure perturbations, computing certificates efficiently via connections to PageRank and Markov decision processes, plus robust training that increases certifiably robust nodes.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness with Additive Noise
papers.summary: Connects adversarial robustness to additive random noise to obtain scalable certified bounds on input perturbation norms, plus a training strategy that enlarges these bounds; on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet it competes with provable defense methods.

papers.title: Certifying Geometric Robustness of Neural Networks
papers.summary: DEEPG certifies robustness to geometric transformations such as rotation and scaling by computing sound, asymptotically optimal linear relaxations for any composition of transformations through sampling plus optimization, certifying more complex transformations than prior methods on large networks.

papers.title: Computing Linear Restrictions of Neural Networks
papers.summary: ExactLine exactly computes the restriction of a piecewise-linear network to a line segment, partitioning it into affine regions; used to find exact ACAS Xu decision boundaries, compute exact integrated gradients and test a hypothesis about adversarial examples.

papers.title: Efficient and Accurate Estimation of Lipschitz Constants for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Computes guaranteed upper bounds on deep network Lipschitz constants via a semidefinite program, modelling activations as gradients of convex potentials with quadratic constraints; gives the most accurate bounds in experiments on random, MNIST and Iris networks, usable for robustness guarantees.

papers.title: Neural Lyapunov Control
papers.summary: Learns nonlinear control policies together with neural Lyapunov functions using a learner and a counterexample-finding falsifier, terminating with provable stability once no counterexample exists, and obtaining much larger regions of attraction than LQR and SOS/SDP.

papers.title: On Relating Explanations and Adversarial Examples
papers.summary: Shows that explanations and adversarial examples of ML models are related by a generalized hitting set duality, and gives algorithms that compute adversarial examples from explanations and vice versa.

papers.title: Preventing Gradient Attenuation in Lipschitz Constrained Convolutional Networks
papers.summary: Trains provably Lipschitz convolutional networks without gradient norm attenuation via BCOP, the Block Convolution Orthogonal Parameterization of orthogonal convolutions, competing with existing approaches for provable adversarial robustness and Wasserstein distance estimation.

papers.title: Provable Certificates for Adversarial Examples: Fitting a Ball in the Union of Polytopes
papers.summary: GeoCert computes exact pointwise robustness of ReLU networks for convex ℓp norms by finding the largest ball around an input inside a polyhedral complex, returning anytime lower bounds that tighten until exact and beat prior work under time limits.

papers.title: Provably Robust Deep Learning via Adversarially Trained Smoothed Classifiers
papers.summary: Improves randomized smoothing by adversarially training smoothed classifiers with an attack adapted to them, outperforming all existing provably ℓ2-robust classifiers on ImageNet and CIFAR-10; pre-training and semi-supervised learning give further gains.

papers.title: Theoretical evidence for adversarial robustness through randomization
papers.summary: Gives theoretical grounding for noise-injection defenses: relates the randomization rate to adversarial robustness for exponential-family noise distributions and derives an upper bound on the adversarial generalization gap of randomized networks, supported by experiments.

papers.title: Tight Certificates of Adversarial Robustness for Randomly Smoothed Classifiers
papers.summary: Extends robustness certificates for randomly smoothed classifiers beyond Gaussian ℓ2 to broad distribution classes, including discrete ℓ0-bounded adversaries, and tightens guarantees using function-class assumptions such as decision trees; evaluated on image and molecule datasets.

months.label: August 2019
months.intro: ASE 2019 decisions: property inference for deep neural networks, extracting formal input and layer preconditions from neuron activation patterns, applied to MNIST and ACAS Xu networks for explanation, robustness guarantees and proof simplification.

papers.title: Property Inference for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Infers formal properties of feed-forward networks from neuron activation patterns, extracting input and layer preconditions that imply output properties; applied to MNIST and ACAS Xu networks for explanation, robustness guarantees, proof simplification and distillation.

months.label: July 2019
months.intro: CCS 2019 and ICCV 2019 decisions: interval bound propagation scales verified training to large image classifiers, and NPAQ quantitatively verifies binarized neural networks with PAC-style guarantees, applied to robustness, trojan attacks and fairness.

papers.title: Scalable Verified Training for Provably Robust Image Classification
papers.summary: Shows that interval bound propagation, with a suitable loss and hyper-parameter schedule, trains large provably robust image classifiers that beat more complex methods on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and SVHN in verified accuracy, and verifies the largest model yet on downscaled ImageNet.

papers.title: Quantitative Verification of Neural Networks and Its Security Applications
papers.summary: NPAQ quantitatively verifies binarized neural networks by estimating how many inputs satisfy a logical property with PAC-style soundness guarantees, applied to quantifying adversarial robustness, trojan attack efficacy and fairness.

months.label: May 2019
months.intro: IJCAI 2019 decisions: Robustra trains provably robust networks over a reference model's adversarial space, while other titles address statistical robustness guarantees for Bayesian neural networks, differential privacy with provable robustness, and counterexample-guided strategy improvement for POMDPs using recurrent neural networks.

papers.title: Counterexample-Guided Strategy Improvement for POMDPs Using Recurrent Neural Networks
Heterogeneous Gaussian Mechanism: Preserving Differential Privacy in Deep Learning with Provable Robustness
Robustra: Training Provable Robust Neural Networks over Reference Adversarial Space
papers.summary: Robustra trains provably robust DNNs by solving the attacker-defender min-max game over a reference model's adversarial space through a linearized dual. On MNIST it cuts the ℓ∞ provable error bound from 2.74% to 2.09% at ε=0.1 and 24.19% to 16.91% at ε=0.3.

papers.title: Statistical Guarantees for the Robustness of Bayesian Neural Networks

months.label: April 2019
months.intro: CAV 2019 and ICML 2019 decisions: the SMT-based Marabou framework appears alongside randomized smoothing with a tight Gaussian ℓ2 guarantee. POPQORN certifies recurrent networks including LSTMs and GRUs, PROVEN takes a probabilistic approach to verification, and non-uniform bounds against adversarial attacks are certified.

papers.title: The Marabou Framework for Verification and Analysis of Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Marabou is an SMT-based framework that verifies deep neural network properties by turning queries into constraint satisfaction problems, supporting various activations and topologies, high-level reasoning to prune search, parallel execution and TensorFlow inputs.

papers.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing
papers.summary: Proves a tight ℓ2 robustness guarantee for randomized smoothing with Gaussian noise, turning any noise-tolerant classifier into a certifiably robust one; reaches 49% certified top-1 accuracy on ImageNet for ℓ2 perturbations below 0.5.

papers.title: On Certifying Non-Uniform Bounds against Adversarial Attacks
POPQORN: Quantifying Robustness of Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.summary: POPQORN computes certified lower bounds on the minimum adversarial perturbation for recurrent networks, including vanilla RNNs, LSTMs and GRUs, handling multi-step inputs and gate-state interactions; per-step robustness quantification gives new insights.

papers.title: PROVEN: Verifying Robustness of Neural Networks with a Probabilistic Approach

months.label: March 2019
months.intro: CVPR 2019 decisions: verification of output-size specifications for machine translation and image captioning models, and robustness verification of classification networks with sigmoid activations via linear programming.

papers.title: Knowing When to Stop: Evaluation and Verification of Conformity to Output-Size Specifications
papers.summary: Studies attacks that lengthen outputs of variable-length models, using a differentiable proxy to find inputs giving outputs 50 times longer, and a verification method that proves output length stays below a bound for machine translation and image captioning models.

papers.title: Robustness Verification of Classification Deep Neural Networks via Linear Programming
papers.summary: Verifies robustness of classification networks with sigmoid activations by recasting it as checking the most suspected input point, a nonlinear optimization relaxed into a linear program; experiments show better precision and scalability on image classifiers.

months.label: February 2019
months.intro: PLDI 2019 decisions: inductive synthesis of programs and invariants to verify and shield reinforcement-learning neural policies, and Charon's combination of gradient-based counterexample search with abstraction-based proof search for local robustness.

papers.title: An inductive synthesis framework for verifiable reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Verifies reinforcement learning neural policies by synthesizing simpler deterministic programs plus inductive invariants through counterexample- and syntax-guided synthesis; the programs monitor the network at runtime and block unsafe actions, with low overhead across cyber-physical applications.

papers.title: Optimization and abstraction: a synergistic approach for analyzing neural network robustness
papers.summary: Charon verifies local robustness of neural networks by combining gradient-based counterexample search with abstraction-based proof search guided by a learned verification policy, giving a sound and δ-complete procedure that outperforms AI^2, Reluplex and Reluval.

months.label: December 2018
months.intro: ICLR 2019 decisions: mixed integer programming gives exact adversarial accuracy for piecewise-linear networks, while training for ReLU stability makes verification faster. Other directions include boosting robustness certification, statistical robustness estimates via multi-level splitting, and verification of nonlinear specifications such as energy conservation in learned dynamics.

papers.title: A Statistical Approach to Assessing Neural Network Robustness
papers.summary: Estimates the probability that a network property is violated under an input model with multi-level splitting, a Monte Carlo rare-event method, giving statistical robustness estimates that emulate formal verification on benchmarks while scaling to larger networks.

papers.title: Boosting Robustness Certification of Neural Networks
Evaluating Robustness of Neural Networks with Mixed Integer Programming
papers.summary: Formulates verification of piecewise-linear networks as a mixed integer program with tight formulations and a presolve step, running two to three orders of magnitude faster and finding the exact adversarial accuracy of an MNIST classifier at ℓ∞ ε=0.1.

papers.title: Training for Faster Adversarial Robustness Verification via Inducing ReLU Stability
papers.summary: Trains networks to be both robust and easier to verify by encouraging weight sparsity and ReLU stability; sparsity makes intractable verification tractable, and ReLU stability adds a 4-13x verification speedup across training procedures and verifiers.

papers.title: Verification of Non-Linear Specifications for Neural Networks
papers.summary: Extends neural network verification to convex-relaxable nonlinear specifications, such as energy conservation in learned dynamics, semantic label consistency under perturbation and bounded errors when summing handwritten digits, and verifies them effectively while exposing failure modes.

months.label: November 2018
months.intro: AAAI 2019 decisions: bound propagation grows with CNN-Cert and RecurJac's Jacobian bounds, alongside verification of RNN-based agent-environment systems. Abduction-based explanations and inverse abstraction of neural network pre-images via symbolic interpolation point toward explanation and interpretable analysis.

papers.title: Abduction-Based Explanations for Machine Learning Models
CNN-Cert: An Efficient Framework for Certifying Robustness of Convolutional Neural Networks
Inverse Abstraction of Neural Networks Using Symbolic Interpolation
papers.summary: Computes compact symbolic over- and under-approximations of neural network pre-images layer by layer via symbolic interpolation, enabling formal analysis, extraction of simple control laws and interpretable descriptions of inputs leading to unsafe outputs.

papers.title: RecurJac: An Efficient Recursive Algorithm for Bounding Jacobian Matrix of Neural Networks and Its Applications
Verification of RNN-Based Neural Agent-Environment Systems
papers.summary: Verifies agent-environment systems whose stateful agent runs a ReLU recurrent network, using equivalences between recurrent and feed-forward networks on bounded traces to give a sound and complete procedure for properties in a simplified bounded LTL.

months.label: October 2018
months.intro: POPL 2019 decisions: DeepPoly, an abstract domain combining floating-point polyhedra and intervals with transformers for ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and maxpool, certifies deep neural networks and, with trace partitioning, robustness to rotations.

papers.title: An abstract domain for certifying neural networks
papers.summary: DeepPoly certifies deep neural networks with an abstract domain combining floating-point polyhedra and intervals, with transformers for affine, ReLU, sigmoid, tanh and maxpool; more precise than prior work, and with trace partitioning it proves robustness to rotations.

months.label: September 2018
months.intro: NeurIPS 2018 decisions: bound propagation and abstract interpretation lead, with CROWN for general activations, DeepZ, symbolic-interval safety analysis and semidefinite relaxations. A unified view of piecewise-linear verification brings a benchmark comparison, while Lipschitz estimation with AutoLip and SeqLip, Lipschitz-margin training and scaled provable adversarial defenses advance certified robustness.

papers.title: A Unified View of Piecewise Linear Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Presents a unified framework covering existing piecewise-linear network verifiers, yielding new combined methods with a two-orders-of-magnitude speedup, and a benchmark dataset used for the first experimental comparison of verification algorithms and problem hardness factors.

papers.title: Efficient Formal Safety Analysis of Neural Networks
papers.summary: Checks safety properties of neural networks, such as L-norm robustness, by estimating tight output bounds over input ranges and finding concrete counterexamples, outperforming existing approaches by orders of magnitude on networks 10 times larger.

papers.title: Efficient Neural Network Robustness Certification with General Activation Functions
papers.summary: CROWN certifies robustness of networks with general activations, including ReLU, tanh, sigmoid and arctan, by bounding activations with adaptively chosen linear and quadratic functions, improving certified lower bounds over Fast-Lin on ReLU networks at similar cost.

papers.title: Fast and Effective Robustness Certification
papers.summary: DeepZ certifies neural network robustness with abstract interpretation sound under floating point, supporting ReLU, tanh and sigmoid in feedforward and convolutional networks; it verifies 97% on an 88,500-unit network under L∞ ε=0.1 in 133 seconds average.

papers.title: Lipschitz regularity of deep neural networks: analysis and efficient estimation
papers.summary: Shows exact Lipschitz constant computation is NP-hard even for two-layer networks, then gives AutoLip, a generic upper bound for any automatically differentiable function, and SeqLip, which tightens bounds for sequential networks by splitting per layer pair.

papers.title: Lipschitz-Margin Training: Scalable Certification of Perturbation Invariance for Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Lower-bounds the adversarial perturbation size needed to fool a network using Lipschitz constants and prediction margins, applicable to complicated architectures, plus Lipschitz-margin training that enlarges provably guarded areas, giving non-trivial guarantees on large networks.

papers.title: Scaling provable adversarial defenses
papers.summary: Scales provable adversarial training to general networks with skip connections and nonlinearities, using random projections and cascades; provable robust error falls from 5.8% to 3.1% on MNIST at ε=0.1 and from 80% to 36.4% on CIFAR at ε=2/255.

papers.title: Semidefinite relaxations for certifying robustness to adversarial examples
papers.summary: Certifies robustness of arbitrary ReLU networks to adversarial examples with a semidefinite relaxation that is tighter than previous relaxations and gives meaningful guarantees on three networks not trained against it.

months.label: May 2018
months.intro: ICML 2018 and USENIX Security 2018 decisions: ReluVal's symbolic interval analysis and Fast-Lin and Fast-Lip certify ReLU networks much faster than Reluplex, while certified training takes shape through the convex outer adversarial polytope and differentiable abstract interpretation.

papers.title: Formal Security Analysis of Neural Networks using Symbolic Intervals
papers.summary: ReluVal checks security properties of ReLU networks without SMT solvers, using parallelizable symbolic interval analysis to bound outputs. It is 200 times faster than Reluplex on average and verifies a property on which Reluplex timed out.

papers.title: Differentiable Abstract Interpretation for Provably Robust Neural Networks
Provable Defenses against Adversarial Examples via the Convex Outer Adversarial Polytope
papers.summary: Trains ReLU classifiers provably robust to norm-bounded perturbations by minimizing worst-case loss over a convex outer approximation of reachable activations, solving the dual LP as a backprop-like network; on MNIST, provable error stays below 5.8% at ℓ∞ ε=0.1.

papers.title: Towards Fast Computation of Certified Robustness for ReLU Networks
papers.summary: Fast-Lin and Fast-Lip certify lower bounds on the minimum adversarial distortion of ReLU networks by linear bounding of ReLUs or local Lipschitz bounds, running over 10,000 times faster than Reluplex, and prove approximation hardness for ℓ1 distortion.

months.label: April 2018
months.intro: IJCAI 2018 decisions: reachability analysis of deep neural networks with provable guarantees.

papers.title: Reachability Analysis of Deep Neural Networks with Provable Guarantees

months.label: January 2018
months.intro: ICLR 2018 decisions: certified training emerges, with a differentiable semidefinite relaxation that certifies and trains one-hidden-layer networks, and principled adversarial training over a Wasserstein ball that certifies distributional robustness.

papers.title: Certified Defenses against Adversarial Examples
papers.summary: Certifies one-hidden-layer networks against adversarial attacks via a differentiable semidefinite relaxation bound that is also optimized during training; on MNIST the resulting certificate guarantees no attack within ε=0.1 per pixel exceeds 35% test error.

papers.title: Certifying Some Distributional Robustness with Principled Adversarial Training
papers.summary: Trains models with distributionally robust optimization over a Wasserstein ball via a Lagrangian penalty, augmenting updates with worst-case data perturbations; for smooth losses this provably gives moderate robustness and certifies robustness of the population loss at low cost.

months.label: November 2017
months.intro: AAAI 2018 decisions: safe reinforcement learning through formal verification with verified runtime monitoring and through shielding, alongside verification of properties of binarized deep neural networks.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Formal Methods: Toward Safe Control Through Proof and Learning
papers.summary: Ensures safe reinforcement learning by combining formal verification with verified runtime monitoring: safety guarantees hold while the agent explores within verified control choices, and on model violations it learns to return to modelled states; demonstrated on adaptive cruise control.

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
Verifying Properties of Binarized Deep Neural Networks

months.label: September 2017
months.intro: NeurIPS 2017 decisions: instance-specific formal lower bounds on adversarial robustness with Cross-Lipschitz regularization, and safe model-based reinforcement learning that learns neural network control policies with Lyapunov stability certificates.

papers.title: Formal Guarantees on the Robustness of a Classifier against Adversarial Manipulation
papers.summary: Gives the first formal instance-specific lower bounds on the input change needed to alter a classifier's decision, and proposes Cross-Lipschitz regularization that improves robustness of kernel methods and neural networks without loss in prediction performance.

papers.title: Safe Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Stability Guarantees
papers.summary: Learns neural network control policies with provable Lyapunov stability certificates using statistical dynamics models with a Gaussian process prior, safely expanding the safe region; optimizes a policy on a simulated inverted pendulum without it ever falling.

months.label: June 2017
months.intro: OOPSLA 2017 decisions: FairSquare certifies fairness of decision-making programs by verifying probabilistic program properties.

papers.title: FairSquare: probabilistic verification of program fairness
papers.summary: FairSquare automatically certifies that decision-making programs meet fairness definitions, encoded as probabilistic program properties, using a new technique for verifying probabilistic properties; it verifies fairness for programs beyond reach of existing program analysis tools.

months.label: April 2017
months.intro: CAV 2017 decisions: complete verification arrives with Reluplex, an SMT solver extending the simplex method to ReLU networks and evaluated on ACAS Xu collision-avoidance networks, alongside safety verification of deep neural networks.

papers.title: Reluplex: An Efficient SMT Solver for Verifying Deep Neural Networks
papers.summary: Reluplex verifies properties of deep ReLU networks, or finds counterexamples, by extending the simplex method to handle the non-convex ReLU; on ACAS Xu collision-avoidance networks it proves properties of networks an order of magnitude larger than before.

papers.title: Safety Verification of Deep Neural Networks

undated.title: AI2: Safety and Robustness Certification of Neural Networks with Abstract Interpretation
Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy
undated.summary: PixelDP certifies robustness to norm-bounded adversarial examples using a connection to differential privacy, the first certified defense that scales to large networks and datasets such as Inception on ImageNet and applies to arbitrary model types.
